Hey folks,
**Don Lemon** joined me live, and we went straight at power, fear, hypocrisy, and what it actually feels like to be targeted for telling the truth. This conversation was raw, funny in dark moments, and deadly serious where it mattered.
**Timestamps:**
* [**00:01:07**] The absurdity of "Free Don Lemon" and why this moment says everything about how broken things are
* [**00:06:18**] Calling out the culture of fear: silencing journalists, chilling protest, abusing power
* [**00:12:39**] Trump's billions vs. people who can't afford eggs, and why the rage is justified
* [**00:20:07**] JD Vance, fake constitutionalists, and the bootlicker problem
* [**00:31:33**] "Too big to rig": why Democrats have to run everywhere and leave no doubt

We talked about Don's arrest, the First Amendment, the cowardice of people who wrap themselves in faith and the flag while shredding the Constitution, and why economic populism is becoming the next battlefield. We also laughed -- because sometimes gallows humor is the only thing that keeps you sane. If you care about press freedom, democracy, and calling bullshit where it lives, this episode is essential. Peter,
Some nights, it’s hard to sleep.
I think about the candidates we endorse. How much they’ve overcome just to get on the ballot. How powerful they could be — if they had the resources.
But here’s what gives me hope:
**More than 15,000 people have signed up to make a monthly donation to Leaders We Deserve.** That consistent support is a game-changer.
**Today, I’m asking you to join them. Even $5 a month makes a real difference.**
**[If you’re ready to help sustain this movement and elect the next generation of leaders, will you start a monthly contribution of any amount right now?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260204_1_sleep.t9bFBc&refcode=em20260204-3120&amount=5&t=4&akid=3120%2E587540%2EA7NwCk)**

Let me explain why monthly donations matter so much:
* **They let us plan ahead.** When we know what’s coming in, we can endorse more candidates, launch ads, and support candidates early.
* **They build early momentum.** Big donors and national orgs watch early fundraising numbers to decide who’s “viable.” Recurring gifts help us show that our candidates are serious — and that they have a movement behind them.
* **They create lasting power.** Sustained donations help us play the long game, because flipping a legislature or building progressive power doesn’t happen overnight.

We don’t take corporate PAC money. We don’t have billionaire donors on speed dial. We have _you_.
****If you’re ready to help elect the next generation of leaders — and if you believe in playing the long game —**[please start a monthly donation today.**](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260204_1_sleep.t9bFBc&refcode=em20260204-3120&amount=5&t=8&akid=3120%2E587540%2EA7NwCk)

David Hogg

name: Ximena, United We Dream
subject: There’s only one way to do it: with love.
body:
Benito said it best: “The only thing more powerful than hate is love.” | | | Hey Peter, Bad Bunny said it best after his Grammy win on Sunday night, “The only thing that is more powerful than hate is love.” Everything we do, from showing up to community-organized protests in below-zero temperature to calling our Senators to demand no more money for ICE, we do it for the love of our communities and our families. In recent weeks, we’ve been carrying heavy emotions: anger, fear, helplessness. We’ve watched our loved ones being dragged out of their homes without a warrant, parents being shot by ICE agents, and our neighbors sent to detention hundreds of miles away from our communities. We feel this way because we care for one another. Now is our time to channel these feelings into something much more powerful. #
Stop the chaos. Hold the line.
Peter, this is what elected leaders must do in the face of an administration that is intent on destroying our democracy for their own gain.
I have spent my career working for North Carolinians. Advocating for more resources for students in public schools and better pay for teachers. Building a clean energy economy to bring good-paying jobs to our communities while protecting this planet. Defending the right to cast a ballot and participate in our democracy. Fighting for Medicaid Expansion and winning it for the people. **I stand ready to do all this and more to deliver for the American people as the next Democratic Senator from North Carolina.**
_Far-right Republicans don’t tend to like that about me — and they don’t want me bringing this fight to Washington._
They’re attacking me in the media — President Trump has even done so from the stage at his rallies. They’re preparing to spend untold sums trying to take me down.

Roy

name: Newt Gingrich
subject: This is not about politics
body:
They need our prayers & our voice
| | | | |
---
Friend,
I want to take you back in history for a moment, and you’ll very quickly understand why.

Forty-seven years ago, in the shadow of Soviet tanks and communist oppression, Pope John Paul II stepped onto Polish soil for the first time in thirty-one years and spoke three simple words:

_**“Be not afraid.”**_

Millions had gathered there in Warsaw’s Victory Square. The regime trembled. And within a decade, the Berlin Wall lay in rubble.

**Paired together with courageous political leadership from Ronald Reagan and Margaret Thatcher,_faith – spoken boldly – had triumphed over fear._**

Today, that same spirit is under siege – not in Poland, but in places like **Nigeria, Sudan and even South Korea.**

**Consider Leah Sharibu, a brave 15-year-old Christian schoolgirl in Nigeria.** In 2018, Islamic State barbarians abducted 110 girls from her school. While 104 were returned and five tragically killed, they kept Leah – as punishment for her **unyielding refusal to renounce Christ and convert to Islam.** Now, many years later, she remains in captivity with ISWAP (Islamic State West Africa Province), who threaten to hold her as a "slave for life."

And yet, this is just one example facing Christians in Nigeria. Since 2009, there have been a reported **19,000 churches destroyed** , **over 100,000 killed** and **at least 5 million more displaced.** The data reveal that for every one Muslim, 5.2 Christians are killed.

**In Sudan** , Islamist paramilitaries known as the Rapid Support Forces have been on a rampage, **bombing churches** , and **killing priests and worshippers sheltering inside while forcing survivors to convert or be killed** – in some cases, **_crucified_**. **Over 150,000 have died in the conflict, many hunted and targeted for their faith.** This ongoing conflict has resulted in a catastrophic humanitarian crisis, including mass displacement, severe food insecurity, and the complete collapse of public services.

**In South Korea** , a nation we rebuilt and have defended for 75 years, the new government with communist sympathies has been **arresting pastors, seizing church records, and even jailed an 82-year-old religious leader for leading prayer.**

And if you think this is only an international problem, I ask you to think back just a couple of years, when **pro-life grandmothers – _women in their 70s and 80s_ – were handcuffed and imprisoned by Joe Biden’s DOJ for peacefully praying outside abortion clinics.**

I don’t share these tragic, gruesome facts to paralyze you with despair, but to rally you to act. And here’s how...

**Save the Persecuted Christians** is an organization that has been effectively fighting on the front lines of this battle – **leading a 200+ group coalition to amplify survivors’ voices, awaken the public and policymakers, and drive direct action to hold the perpetrators accountable.**

In fact, they played a key role in the successful effort to encourage President Trump to designate Nigeria as a “Country of Particular Concern” (CPC), officially laying the groundwork for targeted sanctions and other measures.

I was born in Camden, Arkansas, as the third of three children to my parents, Olive and Charles Tuberville. They raised me to consistently work hard and stand on principle, which I've brought with me every step of my life.

I met my wife, Suzanne, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans in 1989. We married three years later and have two amazing children, Tucker and Troy. _**They continue to make me proud every single day.**_

[](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=dfbd99cd4ce2402a95b74704a94d3d1e&_e=RaVAd4716EAE-_r20GtGGhjlmrlhVHX869UwojrQuk24EJclcriSYKH-X62jQXlivhn1sjcPSLJx-17zCAosGMlIizzEPNFAfcPj7u4nebg4spUb5e_5HX6reAYWr2qci0wUT8sf2GKf2uTFyKJhCVrNCvhSpxGnA0djb66wXoPxOyW7bbacTpd3Q4o4WDpHIFemCComoZ37m28s4-pTt54z5DsDPEUUpZcKl7wyHL-UjKc1t2pH0MMe8iL0tUhbtJT0ff2k8EWKMXphCHqTRXnuED0cq-rszmlkTIsildL6ULn8exEz4WvCrttDQH9OANJ3Icn1TX4BsHsNuVEiwKeXS9t9bUqe9GjtA7ze9qR_i1jaSzzWJYDb6Nk65XrBVQu243p9EnWNFtG65azQY97OCPtM5w6Fw74AhaR9VPXJTVzeW8CIK8l7GTBLgTYh76zolth7SXCkybQ5NO0vMVqXCzcNZGvU5NZ2LvnOZUDKc_0RdQROqWptTZleD39iVYWEJpSoJFhmQYYT4bxbd5TOLlbMWBHK5uYrsgRsF7xHB3UlYYguHaT1KV2pBcz_)
After graduating from SAU, I took my first coaching job at Hermitage High School before graduating to the college level as an assistant coach at Arkansas State University.

Just two years later, I started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, where I went on to become their defensive coordinator. Raising the minimum wage sounds kind. Politicians say a bigger number on a paycheck will lift people out of poverty. But wages don't come from speeches or slogans. They come from the value a worker creates for a customer. When government sets a high, one-size-fits-all floor, it doesn't raise value--it bans low-paid work and hopes the rest sorts itself out.
Who gets hurt first? Beginners. Teenagers, people reentering the workforce, folks with disabilities, and anyone who needs that first rung on the ladder. A small shop might happily hire a 17-year-old at $11 to wash dishes and learn. Make the legal floor $17 and the job doesn't improve; the job disappears. You can't climb a ladder with the bottom step sawed off.
Small businesses take the next hit. Picture a rural diner paying three dishwashers $11 an hour. A mandated jump to $17 is $6 more per hour, per person--about $36,000 a year before payroll taxes and insurance. That owner can't raise prices 50% overnight and keep customers. So they cut hours, eliminate positions, buy a machine, or shut the doors. None of those options helps entry-level workers.
Families and seniors feel it too. Higher labor costs show up as higher prices for groceries, meals, haircuts, childcare, lawn care--everything. Hours get trimmed. Overtime dries up. Perks like free meals, flexible schedules, or paid training quietly vanish. On paper the hourly rate looks better; in real life the paycheck can be smaller.
Nonprofits and local government don't escape. Church daycares, shelters, libraries, and EMS can't raise prices enough to cover big payroll jumps. Taxpayers are told to make up the difference, or services get cut. It's a hidden tax that never appears on a budget line.
Meanwhile, hiring standards ratchet up. If every hour costs more, managers favor already-trained workers and reject anyone with a thin resume or a gap. That hurts minority youth and low-income beginners most--the very people the policy claims to help. And the compliance burden tilts the field toward national chains with legal teams. One lawsuit or back-pay claim that a big company shrugs off can sink a family business. Fewer small competitors mean less choice and, over time, higher prices.
There's a better way to raise pay that doesn't outlaw opportunity. Cut the cost of hiring by lowering or eliminating employer taxes and fees on the lowest wage brackets. Slash needless licenses and paperwork so people can work and small shops can grow. Protect flexible work, tip credits, and part-time on-ramps. And supercharge apprenticeships and career-tech so beginners gain skills fast and become worth more in the market.
Real prosperity comes when workers produce more value and keep more of it, not when politicians write a bigger number on paper. If we care about people at the margins, we should build ladders--skills, experience, and freedom to make a deal--rather than pulling the first rungs out from under them. The minimum-wage promise is simple; the damage is, too. Let's choose policies that actually help everyone climb.

One lawsuit or back-pay claim that a big company shrugs off can sink a family business. Fewer small competitors mean less choice and, over time, higher prices. There's a better way to raise pay that doesn't outlaw opportunity. Cut the cost of hiring by lowering or eliminating employer taxes and fees on the lowest wage brackets. Slash needless licenses and paperwork so people can work and small shops can grow. Protect flexible work, tip credits, and part-time on-ramps. And supercharge apprenticeships and career-tech so beginners gain skills fast and become worth more in the market. Real prosperity comes when workers produce more value and keep more of it, not when politicians write a bigger number on paper. If we care about people at the margins, we should build ladders--skills, experience, and freedom to make a deal--rather than pulling the first rungs out from under them. The minimum-wage promise is simple; the damage is, too. Let's choose policies that actually help everyone climb. Peter, One hundred and twenty-five years ago, Langston Hughes was born in Joplin, Missouri. The grandchild of enslaved people, he came into a world in which Jim Crow laws were spreading rapidly across the United States, forcing racial segregation in schools, libraries, buses, and restaurants, and robbing Black men of the right to vote. And yet, despite the vicious racism he witnessed every day, Hughes imagined a better future for this country. In “Let America Be America Again,” he wrote: _Let America be the dream the dreamers dreamed—
Let it be that great strong land of love
Where never kings connive nor tyrants scheme
That any man be crushed by one above... _ _O, yes,
I say it plain,
America never was America to me,
And yet I swear this oath—
America will be!_ In this ugly, terrible moment in our country, we should take a page from Hughes — **not only dreaming of what America can be in the future, but vowing to help make that dream a reality.** This administration has sunk to unthinkable depths of cruelty and corruption. They’ve tried to break our democracy from the inside, all to amass power and wealth for themselves. But I believe they will ultimately fail. And I plan to tell my kids, and their kids someday, about **what we did in this moment,** when we had to dream big, roll up our sleeves, and get to work. I want to tell them that we didn’t back down for a second in our fight for equality, fairness, and justice. The NDRC is at the forefront of an existential fight for a representative democracy. It's a fight we must win. That requires enough of us showing up and putting in the effort — and yes, make a grassroots donation as you are able to fund this mission-critical work. [**Please stand with us and give what you can to help us protect our democracy and keep it strong for future generations.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124744220/599601582/-2069046819?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_HeartfeltDeadline_email_20260204-NDRC-Tier1-HeartfeltDeadline_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260204-NDRC-Tier1-HeartfeltDeadline_&utm_campaign=HeartfeltDeadline&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5OTFmNzQwLTMyMDItZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=5sW9QO21r7XpLYlQMWSqKaz6KENB-29to98Y8EHW4KM=) And then, in the immortal words of Langston Hughes: _America will be._ Thank you,

**Peter, I’m sorry about Karoline Leavitt.** A few years ago, Karoline Leavitt ran against me for Congress here in New Hampshire. Her campaign was steeped in extreme MAGA rhetoric and zero connection to the actual issues Granite Staters face every day. **Voters saw right through it and rejected her agenda by nearly 10 points.** [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2533?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_baldwin.1D06-e&refcode=AU_STB_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260204_PM2_V1_S1&t=4&akid=5201%2E35263%2ER0C9AC) Unfortunately that race turned into a national audition. Now the same talking points and spin that New Hampshire voters dismissed are being used daily from the White House briefing room. So if you’re wondering how the rest of the country ended up having to listen to Karoline Leavitt, it’s because New Hampshire proved something important first: Her extreme ideas don’t hold up when you put them in front of real voters. But that hasn’t stopped the MAGA machine from trying. **National Republicans are pouring money into New Hampshire because they think they can break through and notch a win here to cling to their Senate majority.** They’ve lined up behind John Sununu, an NRSC-backed candidate who will vote with Donald Trump and MAGA leadership when it matters most. It’s a new candidate reading from the same old playbook. I’ve beaten their playbook before by focusing on kitchen-table issues, standing up for families, and telling the truth. Now I need your help to do it again. [**Will you split $10 between me****and Tammy Baldwin****today to help us keep this Senate seat blue and fight for what matters to Granite Staters?**](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2533?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_baldwin.1D06-e&refcode=AU_STB_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260204_PM2_V1_S1&t=5&akid=5201%2E35263%2ER0C9AC) Granite Staters value independence. # **Wofford to host ‘The Rule of Law’ A candid conversation with Adair Ford Boroughs & The Honorable Sherri Lydon Thursday at 6pm**
---
| |
Wofford will host Adair Ford Boroughs, who served as the US Attorney for South Carolina during the Biden Administration and The Honorable Sherri Lydon who served as the US Attorney for South Carolina during the first Trump Administration on February 5 at 6pm in the Jerome Richardson Theater. This is free and open to the public.
---
[|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=570ea6b5f9&e=edbde6c9b1)
| |
A Candid Conversation is a moderated discussion series featuring perspectives from both sides of the political spectrum in an effort to foster civil discourse and share critical information in the current political landscape. There is no ticketing or pre-registration process. Seating is general admission and doors open at 5:30pm. For questions about accessible seating and entrance to the building, contact Amanda Gilman, special assistant to the president and campus events management coordinator, at [**gilmanaf@wofford.edu**](mailto:gilmanaf@wofford.edu).

|

| |
# Listen to my latest podcast & join our Substack
---
| |
This week I chat with USC Upstate Professor of Sociology, Colby King about the 40% of residents in Spartanburg who are classified as ‘the working poor’ and the policy decisions impacting them and their children.

# March 7 SPCDP Convention
---
| | Join us March 7 for the SPCDP Convention as we organize for the midterms. RSVP on mobilize and join us from 10-12pm at the SCC Downtown Campus Theater.We’ll be joined by local and statewide candidates and unveil our countywide plan.
---
[|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=4c3b285fd4&e=edbde6c9b1)
| [RSVP Here](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=eeb1e91ccb&e=edbde6c9b1)

| |
# Run for office - February 10 info session
---
|
---
| |
We need to challenge every seat in Spartanburg County in 2026. In this past two years we have made incredible strides, and now it's time to move mountains. With over 20 local seats at play we need folks to step up for state house, county council and more.
Our future depends on who shows up to lead. Across South Carolina, we need everyday people ready to flip the future and be a game changer by running for office. Local races matter. Your voice matters. And your leadership could change everything.
Fill out this [**Candidate Interest Form**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a2d3d9c930&e=edbde6c9b1)**and join us for an info session on February 10 at 5:30pm on zoom.** Filing is March 16-30!
---
| |
# Speak out & observe upcoming meetings
---
| |

* February 16 Spartanburg County Council meeting - sign up by noon on Feb 16 same day for County Council Meeting, located at 366 North Church Street.
* February 24 Spartanburg Commission of Public Works Meeting - sign up by noon on Feb 19

* [New data center announcement in Spartanburg County ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=f70867dc1e&e=edbde6c9b1)
* [Corruption fears rise at Spartanburg Water over Collier domination ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=509b1b51b8&e=edbde6c9b1)

* May 30 State Convention

|

|
---
| |

# **Call you state Senator**
---
| |
| | | Even as South Carolina’s [**maternal mortality rate**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=4ae0ee820b&e=edbde6c9b1) continues to rise, lawmakers are advancing House Bill 4760 – a dangerous bill that would**restrict access to medications for abortion, emergency miscarriage care, treatment for postpartum hemorrhage, routine labor and delivery care, and even treatment for common conditions like ulcers and arthritis.**
Earlier today, this bill passed the South Carolina House of Representatives. Now, this cruel bill moves to the Senate. **This threat to our care is real and moving fast.**
**Here’s how you can fight back against H. 4760:**
---
| |
* [**Email:**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=d7a31cfd6c&e=edbde6c9b1) Send a quick, pre-written message to your state senator.
* [**Call:**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=49f7b91334&e=edbde6c9b1) Fill out the form to be immediately connected to your state senator.
* [**Show Up:**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=9cc72ab02e&e=edbde6c9b1) Join us for Reproductive Health Advocacy Day on February 24, where we’ll meet with legislators to discuss the attacks on our health care.

---
|
---
| | | | | |

# **Contact your congressperson and demand they vote no on DHS funding bill**
---
| |
**There are only nine days to go, so we need to act quickly.** Contact your Members of Congress and demand they vote no on any DHS funding bill unless, at a minimum, it:
* Pulls ICE and Border Patrol out of Minneapolis and the rest of our communities
* Prevents ICE or Border Patrol enforcement at designated "sensitive locations" such as houses of worship, day cares, and hospitals
* Restricts ICE and Border Patrol’s ability to target people based on their race, language or accent, place of employment, or location at the time of the apprehension
* Ends the administration’s unlawful practice of warrantless home entry and arrests

**Use our updated call scripts and email tool to contact your Members of Congress today:** [**Call your senators.**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a68792178c&e=edbde6c9b1)****[**Call your representative.**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=b9bf8f7c99&e=edbde6c9b1)****[**Email your Members of Congress**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=527320b99f&e=edbde6c9b1) to drive the point home. [**Check out our explainer**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=d9aeed3951&e=edbde6c9b1) for the latest updates, our full list of demands, and answers to common questions about ICE/CBP funding and a potential shutdown.Keep the pressure on Congress - call you Congressman!
GOP state reps have introduced a bill -- H. 4764 -- to require every county sheriff in the state to agree to a cooperation agreement with ICE. It's bad enough that the Spartanburg County Sheriff's Department last summer signed just such an agreement with ICE. We cannot allow ICE to have a foothold in our state.
There are two things we can do right now: Push county council to rescind the current cooperation agreement. The next meeting is February 16. Fight to get H. 4764 permanently tabled. Call or write to all the members of the state house, Rep Rosalyn Henderson Myers & Travis Moore are on the judiciary committee. [**https://docs.google.com/.../1FdGQGDXSx8z8ap3.../edit...**](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=90d8879741&e=edbde6c9b1)
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| [|
---](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=7b2dd963c7&e=edbde6c9b1)
| |
This past week we attended the OneSpartanburg Legislative Outlook where we were forced to sit through 30 minutes of [Congressman Timmons ](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=a7f72e5f09&e=edbde6c9b1)telling bold faced lies about the administration, calling himself a victim of the housing market, taking us on a weird journey about the health industry, and then ending with defending ICE for murdering two people in Minneapolis. He even admitted Congress has totally lost power and self described his presentation as sounding like an asshole. Don’t believe me - here is the recording. [Timmons Recording](https://kathrynforcongress.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=25ba2d10590e10adb016803dc&id=c2f2d8dac2&e=edbde6c9b1)
Disgraced Senator Josh Kimbrell who is under investigation by the FBI while running for Governor then proceeded to blow hot air for another 30 minutes about his plan for income taxes before he finally and with much fluff and flip flop addressed our measles outbreak. Both officials complained about the gridlock of their legislative bodies because of the very extremist landscape they aided and abetted.
I then joined my parents for the ICE OUT protest downtown and spent the rest of the weekend in the snow with friends and pups.
Stay with me y’all, democracy is a participatory sport.

Republicans have been working overtime to thwart the will of California’s voters — this ruling came after no fewer than six failed attempts — but we beat back every single one of them.
As expected, a perfect losing record for the GOP extremists battling against these lawful election results.
I’m grateful the Supreme Court has made it clear that the will of the voters stands firm. Bottom line: Prop 50 is lawful. That’s why every single challenge against it failed.
I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: when we fight, with the law on our side, we win.
I couldn’t be prouder of my team for successfully defending this ballot initiative in court over and over again on behalf of the Governor and the Secretary of State. It’s moments like this that remind me I’m exactly where I need to be: protecting and defending the rights of the people of this great state.
We know the challenges to our freedoms will keep coming — this administration has been hell-bent on targeting California since day one, and they’re not stopping anytime soon — but I’m more than ready to fight back.

body:
One endorsement doesn’t erase years of fighting for Trump inside Washington.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us10.campaign-archive.com/?e=4d3fe76c62&u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=ca7e3723f8)

| | | | | | Peter,
You’ve probably seen that President Trump has endorsed another candidate in our crowded March 3rd primary.
That endorsement doesn’t change the facts — and it certainly doesn’t change my record.
I remain the **only candidate in this race** who has been working side-by-side with Donald J. Trump since 2016.
I remain the **only candidate** who fought for him every single day through the entire Biden Presidency — from the moment I was sworn in as his FEC Commissioner in 2020 until the day I resigned to run for Congress.
I am also the **only candidate** who has successfully led a federal agency through DOGE-driven reductions, cutting government bloat while delivering real results for taxpayers.
While others were silent or cowering in the dugout, I was inside the federal government[**publicly defending President Trump**](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=931a6611e3&e=4d3fe76c62) in some of the most vicious lawfare attacks ever launched against him.
On the Federal Election Commission, I cast the deciding Republican votes to protect President Trump and his allies in **multiple high-profile enforcement matters** brought by Democrats desperately trying to cripple his movement. Time and again, along with my Republican colleagues, I blocked partisan witch-hunts aimed directly at Donald Trump, his campaign, and his supporters.
**I did it when it was hard.**
**I did it when it was unpopular in Washington.**
**I did it because loyalty matters.**
President Trump may not value that loyalty right now, and that stings — but this race has never been about one man or one endorsement.
This race is about **loyalty to the conservative cause**.
It’s about defending America against the radical Left that wants to tear her down.
It’s about standing firm — without apology — for the America First values that actually **Make America Great Again**.
TX-21 deserves a battle-tested fighter who has already proven he will take on the D.C. swamp, the weaponized bureaucracy, and the never-Trumpers... and win.
I’ve done it before. I will do it again in Congress.
Early voting starts in just under **two weeks** (February 17). Together, we’re going to shock the establishment and win this primary.
Thank you for standing with the one candidate who has never wavered — not once — in the fight for President Trump’s agenda.
For God, For Country, For Trump,
**Trey Trainor** Husband, Father of 6,Proven Conservative Fighter for TX-21
P.S. One endorsement doesn’t erase eight years of unwavering loyalty inside the Trump campaign, on the Trump transition, on the Federal Election Commission — or real executive experience leading DOGE-driven reductions in government. Let’s send Washington a message they’ll never forget.

clean_body: One endorsement doesn’t erase years of fighting for Trump inside Washington. | | | | | | | | | | | | | Peter, You’ve probably seen that President Trump has endorsed another candidate in our crowded March 3rd primary. That endorsement doesn’t change the facts — and it certainly doesn’t change my record. I remain the only candidate in this race who has been working side-by-side with Donald J. Trump since 2016. I remain the only candidate who fought for him every single day through the entire Biden Presidency — from the moment I was sworn in as his FEC Commissioner in 2020 until the day I resigned to run for Congress. I am also the only candidate who has successfully led a federal agency through DOGE-driven reductions, cutting government bloat while delivering real results for taxpayers. While others were silent or cowering in the dugout, I was inside the federal government in some of the most vicious lawfare attacks ever launched against him. On the Federal Election Commission, I cast the deciding Republican votes to protect President Trump and his allies in multiple high-profile enforcement matters brought by Democrats desperately trying to cripple his movement. Time and again, along with my Republican colleagues, I blocked partisan witch-hunts aimed directly at Donald Trump, his campaign, and his supporters. I did it when it was hard. I did it when it was unpopular in Washington. I did it because loyalty matters. President Trump may not value that loyalty right now, and that stings — but this race has never been about one man or one endorsement. This race is about loyalty to the conservative cause. It’s about defending America against the radical Left that wants to tear her down. It’s about standing firm — without apology — for the America First values that actually Make America Great Again. TX-21 deserves a battle-tested fighter who has already proven he will take on the D.C. swamp, the weaponized bureaucracy, and the never-Trumpers... and win. I’ve done it before. I will do it again in Congress. Early voting starts in just under two weeks (February 17). Together, we’re going to shock the establishment and win this primary. Thank you for standing with the one candidate who has never wavered — not once — in the fight for President Trump’s agenda. Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
FEB. 24 IN DALLAS:
TOP's Black History Month Symposium with acclaimed author Michael Harriot
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20BLACK%20AF%20Black%20History%20Month%20event%20with%20Michael%20Harriot.jpg]
TOP is less than a month away from this inspiring evening with Michael Harriot [https://www.michaelharriot.com/] , best-selling author of Black AF History [https://www.michaelharriot.com/poscasts] . Join us as we learn, build community, and celebrate Black history together.
This event – the first of its kind for TOP – takes place during the 100th anniversary of Black History Month and will be held February 24th at Friendship-West Baptist Church in Dallas , so mark your calendars and get your tickets. An RSVP is required to attend this event. [https://topblackhistorysymposium.rsvpify.com/]
https://topblackhistorysymposium.rsvpify.com/ [https://topblackhistorysymposium.rsvpify.com/]
ORGANIZING WIN:
Mobilizing to block a bill that would've given billions more to ICE and Border Patrol
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/ICE%20out.jpg]
PUSHING BACK: U.S. Senators this past Thursday voted against a federal funding package [https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/29/senators-block-funding-package-amid-dhs-standoff-00754927] that contained a Dept. of Homeland Security (DHS) funding bill that would have funneled billions in new tax dollars to ICE and Border Patrol.
TOP members proudly joined our Popular Democracy allies from across the country in calling senators' offices to urge them to block this ridiculous package. What this rapid mobilization showed is that working people in this country want their taxes going toward vital public services, NOT for brutally attacking and demonizing communities.
While this was a big organizing victory, we can't take our foot off the gas pedal. Our country deserves real accountability after the latest terrible acts of these agencies!
THIS MONTH:
TOP healthcare community conversations in Houston and Dallas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20hearts.jpg]
The attacks to healthcare access and affordability in Trump's second term so far have been no joke. From higher health insurance premium costs, to massive cuts to Medicaid, Texans of all walks of life are feeling the negative impacts.
Healthcare is a human right at TOP , and at this critical time with our healthcare system looking bleak, we want to hear from YOU – members, supporters, and community allies. Join at the following free community events in Dallas and Houston, where you can weigh in on what real healthcare looks like to you, and discuss how we can fight for and win that in Texas.
Dallas: Saturday, Feb. 7th, 11 a.m. - 1 p.m.
Contact Eshay at ohutchinson@organizetexas.org [ohutchinson@organizetexas.org] to RSVP.
Houston: Saturday, Feb. 14th, 11 a.m. - 1 p.m.
Contact Lucinda at ldavis@organizetexas.org [ldavis@organizetexas.org] to RSVP.
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfoc1OUiuz2TfuWAMFfFO2p2m3ti1xB9QGZzEjIya3BgLA9EA/viewform [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfoc1OUiuz2TfuWAMFfFO2p2m3ti1xB9QGZzEjIya3BgLA9EA/viewform]
TRUMP TRACKER:
"Tariff Man" is making life less affordable
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Trump%20red%20shadow.png]
We’re back with another installment of our Trump Tracker , where we’re applying Critical Ignoring [https://www.epi.org/publication/47-ways-trump-has-made-life-less-affordable-in-his-first-year/] to help us fight the right-wings’s “flood the zone” [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-echoing-project-2025-flood-zone-strategy-push/story?id=121124118] strategy, so we can focus on the core issues that are top of mind for our communities in this crucial midterm year.
Just over a year into Trump 2.0, and our country's economic forecast is the gloomiest it's been in over a decade. The volatile stock market is one thing, but what's truly hurting families is this regime's reckless policy moves that are further enriching the ultra-wealthy at the expense of everyone else.
When you combine these shameless tax cuts for billionaires with the slashing of public services, stagnant wages, and absurd tariffs, you have a recipe for disaster.
Read up on the dozens of ways how Trump is making life more expensive for working people in this country. [https://www.epi.org/publication/47-ways-trump-has-made-life-less-affordable-in-his-first-year/]

VICTORIA ORGANIZATIVA:
Movilización para bloquear un proyecto de ley que habría otorgado miles de millones de dólares adicionales a ICE y Border Patrol
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/ICE%20out.jpg]
RESISTIENDO: El jueves pasado, los senadores estadounidenses votaron en contra de un paquete de financiación federal [https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/29/senators-block-funding-package-amid-dhs-standoff-00754927] que incluía un proyecto de ley de financiación para el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) que habría destinado miles de millones de dólares de los contribuyentes a ICE y a la Patrulla Fronteriza.
Miembros de TOP se unieron con orgullo a nuestros aliados de Popular Democracy de todo el país para llamar a las oficinas de los senadores y exigirles que bloquearan este paquete absurdo. Esta rápida movilización demostró que la gente trabajadora de este país quiere que sus impuestos se destinen a servicios públicos esenciales, NO a atacar y demonizar brutalmente a las comunidades.
Aunque esta fue una gran victoria organizativa, no quitar el pie del acelerador. ¡Nuestro país merece una verdadera rendición de cuentas después de los terribles actos de estas agencias!
ESTE MES:
Las conversaciones de TOP importantes sobre atención médica en Houston y Dallas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20hearts.jpg]
Los ataques al acceso y la asequibilidad de la atención médica durante el segundo mandato de Trump han sido muy graves. Desde el aumento de las primas de los seguros médicos hasta los recortes masivos a Medicaid, los Texanos de todos los ámbitos sociales están sufriendo las consecuencias negativas.
En TOP, consideramos que la atención médica es un derecho humano, y en este momento crítico, con un sistema de salud en una situación precaria, queremos escucharlos a USTEDES: miembros, simpatizantes y miembros de la comunidad. Únanse a los siguientes eventos comunitarios gratuitos en Dallas y Houston, a compartir su opinión sobre cómo debería ser una atención médica digna y discutir cómo podemos luchar por ella y lograrla en Texas.
Dallas: Sábado, 7 de febrero, de 11 a.m. a 1 p.m.
Para confirmar su asistencia, comuníquese con Eshay a ohutchinson@organizetx.org [ohutchinson@organizetx.org] .
Houston: Sábado, 14 de febrero, de 11 a.m. a 1 p.m.
Para confirmar su asistencia, comuníquese con Lucinda a ldavis@organizetx.org [ldavis@organizetx.org] .
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf1bY_DlK7WwjhHEWsdJhb8yQSqAUdL3z_EEH_QepPF2HeAEw/viewform [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf1bY_DlK7WwjhHEWsdJhb8yQSqAUdL3z_EEH_QepPF2HeAEw/viewform]
SEGUIMIENTO A TRUMP:
El "Hombre de los aranceles" está haciendo la vida menos asequible
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Trump%20red%20shadow.png]
Regresamos con otra entrega de nuestro Seguimiento a Trump , donde aplicamos la estrategia de Ignorancia Crítica [https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/misinformation-desk/202511/critical-ignoring-a-strategy-for-information-overload] para combatir la estrategia la derecha de “inundar la zona” [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-echoing-project-2025-flood-zone-strategy-push/story?id=121124118] y así poder enfocarnos en los temas claves que preocupan a nuestras comunidades en este año crucial de elecciones de medio término.
A poco más de un año del inicio de la segunda etapa de Trump, el pronóstico económico de nuestro país es el más sombrío en más de una década. La volatilidad del mercado bursátil es preocupante, pero lo que realmente perjudica a las familias son las políticas imprudentes de este gobierno, que enriquecen aún más a los ultra ricos a costa de todos los demás.
Si combinamos estas descaradas reducciones de impuestos para los multimillonarios con los recortes en los servicios públicos, los salarios estancados y los aranceles absurdos, tenemos la receta perfecta para el desastre.
Infórmese sobre las numerosas maneras en que Trump está encareciendo la vida de la clase trabajadora en este país. [https://www.epi.org/publication/47-ways-trump-has-made-life-less-affordable-in-his-first-year/]

name: Case Dixon
subject: Door Knocking Instructions & Canvassing Link
body:
**Hey everyone** ,

First, thank you again for your support of the campaign. I truly appreciate it.

Several folks have volunteered to help with door knocking, and I also wanted to share this information more broadly for anyone who may be interested in helping, even on an occasional or one-time basis. There is absolutely no obligation. Any amount of help matters and is appreciated. Every conversation matters in a grassroots campaign like this.

**Getting Set Up to Canvass**
Below is the link you’ll use to get set up for canvassing. This tool provides walking routes and shows you exactly which houses to knock.

Canvassing link: [ https://vottiv.app/join/3PHZC4](https://vottiv.app/join/3PHZC4)

How to get started:
1. Click the link, enter your name, and contact information
2. Click “Start Canvassing”
3. Select a route
4. Open the map and begin canvassing

**Campaign Literature**
Before heading out, please coordinate a time to meet with me so I can get you the campaign literature to hand out. You can call or text me at **(205) 282-9103** , and we’ll find a time and place that works.

**What to Say at the Door**
Please keep it simple. The main goals at each door are to:
* Introduce Case Dixon
* Let them know I’m running for U.S. Congress as a Republican
* Share when Election Day is (May 19)

No long pitch is needed, brief and friendly is perfect.

**Best Times to Door Knock**
To maximize the chances of catching people at home:
* Weekdays: anytime between 4:00–6:00 PM
* Saturdays: anytime between 10:00 AM–5:00 PM
* Sundays: please do not door knock

**If No One Is Home**
If no one answers:
* Mark in the app that you knocked but no one was home.
* Leave the campaign literature in an obvious place, but somewhere it won’t blow away (door handle, between the door and frame, under a mat, etc.)

**Weekly Goals & Flexibility**
For those who’ve committed to one shift per week, the goal is to work toward 50–100 doors per week. It may take a couple of weeks to get up to speed, and that’s completely fine.
We also understand that not everyone can door knock every single week. All help matters, and we’re grateful for whatever time you’re able to give.

**Routes, Tracking, and Follow-Up**
Please be sure to mark every house you knock, whether someone comes to the door or not. The app will allow you to specifically mark whether someone answered or not.

If you don’t finish a route, no problem at all. You can:
* Pick back up on the same route next time, or
* Select a different route when you go out again

The most important thing is that all knocked houses are marked in the app, so we avoid repeat visits to the same homes.

**Future Door-Knocking Weekends**
In the future, there will be specific weekends where we may reach out to everyone on the email list, even those who haven’t committed to weekly door knocking, to help us reach a specific goal over a short time frame.

**Thank you** again for being part of this effort. I’m grateful to have you on the team. If you have any questions whatsoever, please don't hesitate to reach out.

In Liberty,
**Case Dixon**
****
Dixon for Congress
(205) 282-9103
615 Brooklane Dr. #3218
Hueytown, AL 35023-2508
DIXONFORUSCONGRESS.COM

Best Times to Door Knock To maximize the chances of catching people at home: Weekdays: anytime between 4:00–6:00 PM Saturdays: anytime between 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Sundays: please do not door knock If No One Is Home If no one answers: Mark in the app that you knocked but no one was home. Leave the campaign literature in an obvious place, but somewhere it won’t blow away (door handle, between the door and frame, under a mat, etc.) Weekly Goals & Flexibility For those who’ve committed to one shift per week, the goal is to work toward 50–100 doors per week. It may take a couple of weeks to get up to speed, and that’s completely fine. We also understand that not everyone can door knock every single week. All help matters, and we’re grateful for whatever time you’re able to give. Routes, Tracking, and Follow-Up Please be sure to mark every house you knock, whether someone comes to the door or not. The app will allow you to specifically mark whether someone answered or not. If you don’t finish a route, no problem at all. You can: Pick back up on the same route next time, or Select a different route when you go out again The most important thing is that all knocked houses are marked in the app, so we avoid repeat visits to the same homes. Future Door-Knocking Weekends In the future, there will be specific weekends where we may reach out to everyone on the email list, even those who haven’t committed to weekly door knocking, to help us reach a specific goal over a short time frame. Thank you again for being part of this effort. I’m grateful to have you on the team. If you have any questions whatsoever, please don't hesitate to reach out. In Liberty, Case Dixon Dixon for Congress (205) 282-9103 615 Brooklane Dr. #3218 Hueytown, AL 35023-2508 DIXONFORUSCONGRESS.COM

Thanks to support from parents, grandparents, and concerned citizens just like you, we started hosting Godly and patriotic “Story Hours” of our own.And now, THOUSANDS of children and parents can gather to pledge allegiance to our flag, read wholesome books, and pray together in their libraries.It’s encouraging to see we can win when we fight back! And the Left will try to bury _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ at every turn. In 2023, Lauren Boebert, made national headlines for the massive disturbance she caused at a showing of the Beetlejuice Musical.
She belligerently hit her weed vape pen in the theater, was on her phone, and when asked by theater staff to leave the theater she loudly hit them with the "do you know I am." But as ridiculous of a scene she made, at least the evening appeared to be an expense she paid for herself.
Now Boebert has been caught spending over $6000 in campaign donor money on traveling to and attending a Kid Rock concert in Texas:

This year Boebert's campaign has reported its lowest ever fundraising haul and it's clear why. Her donors know that this money isn't going to anything political and they've stopped giving.
Her campaign's cash flow has gotten so bad that when it came out that the campaign had received contributions from a vicious ponzi scheme that defrauded hundreds of families, as of August 27, 2025, the campaign had yet to return the contributions.
Boebert is out of money, her supporters are abandoning her, and her voters view her as a carpetbagger with no ties to her new district. There is blood in the water. If there was ever an election where she could be beaten it is this one.

subject: A Virginia You Can Afford
body:

| |

| Friends-
On Tuesday, we met at the General Assembly to roll out our "Virginia You Can Afford" Agenda to lower costs for hardworking people.
---
| |
---
| (Left to Right: Delegate Briana Sewell, Delegate Dan Helmer, Senator Schuyler VanValkenburg, Ryan O'Toole of Freedom Virginia, Delegate Shelly Simonds, and Impacted Virginian Becky Winstead-Roberts)
The Agenda is a 5-part plan to lower costs and ensure Virginia is a place that hardworking people can afford. It will:

* Lower the Cost of Medicine through the Affordable Medicine Act

* Ensure Access to Affordable Housing by boosting home construction so people can afford the home of their choice

* Invest in Affordable Child Care through a Dedicated Child Care Funding Formula

* Make Energy More Affordable by increasing the supply of energy through solar generation

* Ease the burden on hardworking people through middle-class tax cuts

---
| |
---
| (Impacted Virginian Becky Winstead-Roberts speaks on her experience with unaffordable prescription drugs)
"My husband was in the hospital for a stroke- There was a gentleman who was in the hospital with him who had also had a stroke. He had worked for a mom-and-pop company that was not able to afford insurance for him. The man suffered a stroke and ended up on disability for the rest of his life when all he needed was a trip to the doctor and affordable medicine. This led to greater health problems, and now he will be on disability for the rest of his life. [...] While we talk about the cost of medicine, we sometimes don't talk about what it costs us by not having affordable medicine, by not having good access to healthcare. Not only will the Affordable Medicine Act save Virginians money, but it will also save them their health and well-being." -Becky Winstead-Roberts, Impacted Virginian
Thank you to Senator Schuyler VanValkenburg, Delegate Dan Helmer, Delegate Briana Sewell, Delegate Shelly Simonds, and impacted Virginian Becky Winstead-Roberts for joining us in the fight for an affordable Virginia.
---

A teacher in Clinton giving $50. Together, we're going to prove that Americans will stand up for what's right. ## 700 ICE Agents Are Leaving Minnesota
Border czar Tom Homan announced Wednesday the Trump administration will [withdraw 700 federal immigration officers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-OszAQBPCnMR3ILGCHwsXX0OVrr0SOvYQ9-Q8ym1h5-xP3CtdMM9JvpPm6r3dLgdLzv41oeMtrwnoGZMaykkNfbPW5JrfTcR6FHLoX2xUkqFZCK6fVWwqfdWy82RABhwZNr7WE26zGudlNP-jHtMFNjSNqPzw2bVGhnZWbETS6hsylSZBT30sNt06qufe2l1oOuMHkxCjRE-fSfWdKvOMWPvmNpXM5NsHszMcphn8CFgFLrbVz6eGuUsBy0QIWCVeMAhYur3i0e442tZFSwjOzbclhSzHSs1imnLqdY2iK8UelEOhUWozyGS2F303-01FvAz8BAAD__wo5fEU) from Minnesota effective immediately, leaving about 2,000 agents in the state. Homan announced the 25% reduction after touting "unprecedented cooperation" from Minnesota county jails to transfer immigration suspects to ICE before release. President Trump said he learned the administration could use "[a little bit of a softer touch](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkT3O2zAMQE8jbwpk2bHjwUOKwp2-Di3QjgYj0RZb_RgS8wm5feFcodsDHkDikb8_1g8gT3H_DgFn3tIasRaPzJhXMmgzVJtqNI6OcmQyaJ4Mq1Z6kEpLdV0tkH-tfWPnDVFj1-DcjqPSt2nop8bNHeJNt6NFHB4w3R4w9lcLk5n64TEM29TQfE5TWl3bVo36dlHD1Fpo1ag63PTViF6hJU758idRZIebf6VPzBeTQuNnx3wU0d2FXoReaq2XUOLphF4wymcRejmjhF7ezPkZDlngVSSFQHsGphSlyWD-nqkyItoiS9oYs-T0NE5WYnfi7mRhiAYlvK1FsP4lA8WIcCRPRRaXElPcz1WQ5f3e_vqmfnSiW5IhK7qvX85rYy0_MR9Nnu1RyXsqwyh6tQcg_-7i_3rG56z_BQAA__8ROqJ2)" on immigration enforcement following the backlash. The [partial drawdown](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMuq3DAQRL9G3mmQ2w_ZCy8mD-9uIASSpVGktqeDHkbquWL-PjjkD-6uqKKK4vx6294MeYrHNxNw4T1tEWvxyIx5I4sum-pSjfZBZzkzWbRPNhsoGKUCqYbNGfKvrW_csiMCdg0urdYKpnns5-axtL-H3Q4WJsB-GGan9dhhO43aGJhRTw0t15oCNbSt0jDd1Di3zrRKqw53GKzoFTrilG9_EkV-4O5f6R3zzabQ-OXBfBbR3QWsAtZa6y2UeGUCVozyWQSsZ_LEZC95XNUYMLKAlfMznNK4QJEKZ8OUojyf_iIitVKSQqDjv28OjFzknlOQgWLEktgIWE2W93v78-vn773o1mTJie7Lp4sp1vID89nkxZ2VvKcyatGrIxjy_97zh5C_L_A3AAD__5jIl5U) comes after federal agents killed two U.S. citizens during separate January altercations in Minneapolis. The Department of Homeland Security initially defended the killings before the administration moderated its tone as public opinion soured.
## Washington Post Cuts One-Third of Staff
_The Washington Post_ [laid off roughly one-third](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAURp9GOw0gylBQbGM3225p7sBF7gbBADPGt9_MvsLff_lyzvnz3J5AkdL-Gw40zect4VUjtoZlI4uuwOXylWygs56FLNp3g00wsQxMDGzeHFC8N9k74xEFTj0arhQTD71I3QejJF8Wxb1-OcWlnV8apOdcKf0CPy1TT-b7xgSbOWdKPEa2aO6AM8Um9GK2nWToqOUy_s2UWkAf7_zBMtp89NGE1s7aTb86sXZi9ZQgWRxvCDl_F51Yv0qdWC-ogdLechrOXNvwTg7LnintQ6U9kScLqQ0R7ux9HbhketJcqzG0I_bFuPOiGKkuqpNsP4Dif4L2o2wfI_4FAAD__4iigkQ) of its employees on Wednesday in what former executive editor Martin Baron described as one of the darkest days in the newspaper's 150-year history. Executive Editor Matt Murray announced the "strategic reset" would end the current sports desk, restructure local coverage, reduce international reporting to about 12 bureaus. The plan also eliminates the books desk, and suspend the flagship podcast _Post Reports_. The [Jeff Bezos-owned paper](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAUhZ9GOw1eRcaCYhu72XZLc4HreDcIBpgh8_Yb9xX--pyck-_789yeyJ7D6zeepMset0A1eyqF0saWXMLqYg324CtfiS3Zd8ENBMydgE7IzSH77za1Tu9EQGNLelBKwGOZp6U9tJXLgmilm6yaDc5GjUbuchFGDqNRpmV9rwkQchiEgkcv5mVwOAglRtpB2mYS5LjE1P-NHMpBu__GD6XexrP1-ijlys34q4G1gbXW2gdjb4o7b2A178yBcm5gPckx3iXMB4dXiaG7Yi6dx2_c99zlK6aSu2QDglSjnNqk3VXZe86zaibxOpH9_9_yI1kfDf8CAAD__0UCf4M) has struggled with declining revenue despite the Amazon founder's $260 billion net worth as the world's fourth-richest person. The Washington Post Guild said 400 people have left the staff in the past three years. _(Editor's Note: While readers are rejecting partisan legacy media outlets like the Washington Post, The Flyover continues to grow, topping 4 million readers last week for our family of newsletters, as people embrace new platforms offering an unbiased take on the news.)_
## Minute Maid Ends Frozen Juice Era
Minute Maid is [discontinuing its frozen juice concentrates](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuhDAQAL_GdKBleRcu0tBd2pTI2OtjL8ZGsBy6fH10-YX0oxlpvm7TzXDgeP80K2nxaYp0HYFEaJ_YktvN5dIV7cLbse1syZ5iJgRsc8AcmskZDq-pzpz2REhVRrrsOsB-aOshW7TrfEU0D94jDK13Dcx9NzRmhqqtZl9lrN82QGjKEjrsC2iH0pkSOqjIY2NVDeRY0l48EkdZyIdXetJe2LRmQS8i26GqD4WjwvG6rkIWEvNN6ZQ3onBEGBDLXuG4cjyF8tWwy_2efijmj5Mt5Y4Pm6JwPMkpHLNdu-3iEPhoO1XDfTUc_oLyr0tPjb8BAAD__1LSfC4) after 80 years, ending production of the iconic canned juices that became an American breakfast staple for generations of families. The Coca-Cola Company cited shifting consumer preferences as the reason for phasing out flavors including orange juice, lemonade, limeade, pink lemonade, and raspberry lemonade by April. The frozen concentrate [originated during World War II](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkcGq2zwQRp9G3k2Qxo6dLLzIz4835XZTaOnKKNIonlt7ZCT5ivTpSy59gy4_PjhwOD_e5jfLK8vjq91oLCHOQjWvVAqlmR35ZKuPVdzCe94TO3JHsTNq7EEj6PPsLa_PuWv8GIiQ2oZGMwwaL9e-uzbLGOyVutb3pr_jYKzD1rfmToh3PfT2PjQ8vmga9dkYPeDlpPur8dboQbcU8OxUp8lzien0HlnKQmF9xg9KJxe3Zh2XUvas2pvCSeFUaz1tWV6fwokEjqxwCjF6K94nll9_58tT4ZRJCm8kxa4QrGTY4pEEykJA4iEG2FiOQrBZ9pCBXRR2EFL8TQLOipCH94MdZbChUIKLhifZlIHhkajCsUP8BGZSONkEt5v5PpmfX1Q7Rcdetf__9wpANX-jtDdp9HvldeXcD6rTj83y-qla_qnPx4h_AgAA__8niaeg) as an alternative to lemon crystals given to soldiers for vitamin C, launching the Minute Maid brand in 1946. Nostalgic fans flooded social media with memories of watching parents mix the frozen slush or eating it straight from the can. The company said it will focus on [ready-to-drink beverages](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkcGumzAQRb_G7CYyBkKyYJG2YtXXTaV2iUaecTKvMEa2eSj5-oqqf_CWV1e60jn399v0hjKL3n_gwkMJcVLe88ylcJrEMyXcKe7qH7LmNYlnvxWcnHVnsA5sNxHK_JzaiobA7LipeKj73rrL9dxeq8fA1464C7b2tsOefaC-4dZSY1vfYNNXMhxr1tmurm3vLid7vtaEte1tw8F13rSWSUpMp_coWh4c5mf84HTycanm4VHKmk1zM240btz3_bRkPTrjRlbYsnFjiJFQiZLon__x4DRuXES3wrCgEEgGkuyjFtFN9A5SMoQUX6zgUZUJ3jfxnAFD4QQXC0_GlAGVIKBmwMQQmA-hoDEXnO_ijRsxwe1W_7p9fX03zRi9kGm-fTm0855_clqrNNC6yzxLPvemtfcFZf4HWD71ysfg_gYAAP__QOyk2Q) as American tastes shift away from frozen concentrates.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC.
