# Trump Accounts to take center stage at the Super Bowl
A high-profile Super Bowl ad funded by Invest America will **[promote Trump accounts during Sunday's pre-game broadcast,](https://substack.com/redirect/c60f3187-3ded-4d00-b237-7aab129f402a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** highlighting a new government-backed investment program that gives every eligible American child a $1,000 seed deposit to grow tax-free until age 18. With over one million families already signed up, the spot aims to drive massive awareness for the initiative ahead of Super Bowl 60 between the Seahawks and Patriots.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c60f3187-3ded-4d00-b237-7aab129f402a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Massive Awareness Push:** [The 30-second ad, airing on NBC right before kickoff,](https://substack.com/redirect/2441b0c1-3f0e-4414-b15e-a0502826cd44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) features children touting "free money" in pre-funded accounts as part of a major campaign including Times Square billboards and summits.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/799bccab-f7aa-4ca5-83b0-7ab67abbc942?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **Key Program Details:** Eligible kids born 2025-2028 receive a one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit on July 4, invested in a diversified U.S. stock index, with funds locked until age 18 to encourage long-term wealth building.
* **Extra Funding Incentives:** Philanthropists like Michael Dell (pledging $6.25 billion for lower-income grants) and celebrities such as Nicki Minaj, plus employer matches aim to boost accounts beyond the government seed.
* **Growth Projections Cautioned:** White House estimates suggest the $1,000 could compound to $243,000 by age 55 at historical returns.

# Bitcoin crashes below $70,000 barrier
Bitcoin plunged below $70,000 on Thursday for the first time since November 2024, **[sinking as low as $65,562](https://substack.com/redirect/eb6c8a61-ad6e-43aa-ad68-383df93e70fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **amid a brutal crypto sell-off fueled by fading investor confidence and broader risk-asset weakness, with the token now down more than 45% from its October peak above $126,000.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eb6c8a61-ad6e-43aa-ad68-383df93e70fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Key Psychological Breach** : $70,000 shattered as a critical support level, with analysts warning a sustained break could accelerate declines toward $60,000-$65,000 range.
* **Massive Weekly Losses** : Bitcoin is down nearly 17% in five days on pace for its worst week since late 2022, while Ether and Solana also post steep drops of 23-24%.
* **Institutional Reversal** : U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs shifted from heavy buyers a year ago to net sellers in 2026, signaling waning traditional investor interest.
* **Failed Hedge Narrative** : Once touted as digital gold, Bitcoin has underperformed surging precious metals and instead has moved in lockstep with risk-on assets amid geopolitical and macro uncertainties.

# **Silver crashes 12%, a renewed slide after its brief bounce**
Silver prices **[plunged as much as 16%](https://substack.com/redirect/468c99d2-e69b-4544-8fff-6cf4b37eec4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Thursday, resuming a sharp downward trajectory after a fleeting two-day rebound, with spot silver dropping nearly 12% to around $77.42 per ounce amid intense volatility and unwinding of speculative positions built during its 146% surge in 2025.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/468c99d2-e69b-4544-8fff-6cf4b37eec4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Speculative Unwind Accelerates** : Leveraged bets and momentum trading reversed violently, triggering stop-losses, dealer hedging shifts, and cascading losses, per Goldman Sachs, amplifying the sell-off beyond gold's milder 2% dip.
* **Volatility Likened to Memes** : Silver's wild swings drew comparisons to GameStop-style retail frenzy, with excessive speculation detached from fundamentals, and Western investor flows driving the build-up and rapid unwind.
* **Margin Hikes Curb Excess** : Exchanges like CME Group raised requirements post-sell-off to dampen speculation, potentially flushing out remaining leveraged positions before any stabilization.
* **Industrial Demand Persists** : Despite the correction, silver's strong long-term outlook holds due to key uses in solar, electronics, and tech, with analysts advising caution until speculative froth clears.

* * *
* * *
# AI rivals clash as Super Bowl ad war explodes
Anthropic intends to **[unleash Super Bowl ads mocking OpenAI](https://substack.com/redirect/6a2a9f40-7bff-4791-8585-f91c7d0637ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and their plan to introduce labeled ads in ChatGPT, vowing to keep its Claude chatbot ad-free. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman fired back on X, calling the campaign deceptive and dishonest while defending his company's approach as user-respecting, intensifying the fierce rivalry between the two AI powerhouses ahead of Sunday's big game.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6a2a9f40-7bff-4791-8585-f91c7d0637ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Rivalry Roots Exposed** : Anthropic, founded by ex-OpenAI researchers, positions Claude as the pure ad-free alternative in its pregame and in-game spots targeting ChatGPT's upcoming monetization shift.
* **Altman 's Fiery Rebuttal** : Sam Altman admitted laughing at the ads but slammed them as "clearly dishonest" and "doublespeak," insisting OpenAI would never insert intrusive, response-altering promotions.
* **Ad Depiction Controversy** : Anthropic's commercials dramatize "betrayal" by showing fictional ad-riddled chatbots interrupting personal queries with jarring sponsorships, exaggerating OpenAI's labeled bottom-of-response format.
* **Business Model Divide** : Altman countered that Anthropic targets wealthy users with pricey access while OpenAI reaches more free users, framing the dispute as differing paths in the booming AI competition.

Over the last century, free-market capitalism and socialism have provided the dominant interpretations

Over the last century, free-market capitalism and socialism have provided the dominant interpretations, and conflicting visions, of political and economic freedom.
| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zdonj4o33bmn7u5ovb2sb6ua2uojtv1c88bb2ql0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cpj62oj2c9h2bs)
---
| | Dear Friend,Over the last century, free-market capitalism and socialism have provided the dominant interpretations, and conflicting visions, of political and economic freedom. In the past few years, we've seen a growing trend among young Americans in favor of socialism and against capitalism.
---
| [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zq3skhlg08cu1n2o121e7vdnd082gh1b728dmd78_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cpj62oj2c9h2bs)
---
| | **But do they truly understand the history and outcomes of socialism and capitalism?** This is _precisely_ why we put together this brand new eBook, **[_The History Of Socialism And Capitalism_](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zdhedv594kkupimjashga7if1ivt91fcjk24tct0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cpj62oj2c9h2bs)**[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z6uov9ecu6451fqth24fnnpg560hs4ehbn9bi4qo_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cpj62oj2c9h2bs), from Hoover Institution senior fellows Niall Ferguson and Victor Davis Hanson. This eBook consists of two papers--one from each scholar--written in conjunction with _The Human Prosperity Project on Socialism and Free-Market Capitalism_. This project provides objective and scholarly analyses of free-market capitalism, socialism, and hybrid systems and provides evidence on the effectiveness of the various systems on outcomes that affect prosperity and well-being. I think you will find this new eBook particularly important and timely, given the recent interest in policies that are radical from a US historical perspective, some of which are advocated by political leaders. **[Simply click here to request your free copy of _The History Of Socialism And Capitalism_.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zen5h64uv47a40vol3fcauqbbqked439cul4d020_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cpj62oj2c9h2bs)** Thanks,Greg Greg Stamps | Online DevelopmentHoover Institution | Stanford University
---

Over more than one hundred years, Hoover's work has directly led to policies that have produced greater freedom, democracy, and opportunity in the United States and around the world._

| | Fellow Patriot,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

It's not a culture war manifesto.

It's a call to stop.

To rest. To breathe. To return to God.

**Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. **

Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away.

Trust that God is in control.

Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship.

**In _Stop, in the Name of God,_ you'll discover: **

🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout

🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer

🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation

Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again.

That's the heartbeat of his final message.

clean_body: | | | | | Fellow Patriot, | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud. He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus. He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness. And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible. I saw it up close -- Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything. He started observing the Sabbath. Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance. But as an act of obedience. As a way of saying, " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped. He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield. No email. No media. No work. He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children. It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much. But over time, it changed him. And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned... This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust. A book not about politics... but about peace. It 's called: Stop, in the Name of God. Fellow Patriot, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book. It's not a culture war manifesto. It's a call to stop. To rest. To breathe. To return to God. Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away. Trust that God is in control. Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. Fellow Patriot, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage. These are the very things Charlie gave his life for. May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God... A stronger love for your family... And a renewed peace in your own soul. body:
Every single child carries boundless potential, and one of the biggest reasons I’m running for Congress is because I want Iowa to be the best place in the country to help that potential grow.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124795997/599728895/-975735282?refcode=em_logoheader&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMjkyZjNkOS1jMTAyLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gdyD3rqg0DX40i2x3ANssfr6573UQn524Xm9HdnfMNE=)

Peter,

If you ever ask me what set me on the course for a good future, my answer will always be the same: Public schools and teachers gave me every opportunity I’ve ever had.

I am who I am today because educators saw potential in me, pushed me to do better, and held me accountable when I needed it. When an educator invests in a student, it can change the entire course of their life. **Every single child carries boundless potential, and one of the biggest reasons I’m running for Congress is because I want Iowa to be the best place in the country to help that potential grow–to be number one in education again.**

That’s why last week meant so much to me. I had the chance to visit City High and speak with an American government class. The students were so thoughtful and engaged that I forgot I was talking to high schoolers and not my law students. They asked smart questions and reminded me just how bright our future can be.

**But here’s the hard truth: Iowa is ranked 23rd in education. That didn’t happen by accident.** While our schools struggle for resources, Mariannette Miller-Meeks has done nothing to turn things around. She has supported diverting public education funds to private entities, voted for policies that threatened the jobs of up to 145,000 teachers and school staff, and backed cuts totaling more than $35 million from public education funding. _This is unacceptable._

In Congress, trust that I will be a champion for public education, and if anyone dares to go against Iowa's public schools, I. Will. Raise. Hell. Funding public education with public dollars is nonnegotiable.

clean_body: Every single child carries boundless potential, and one of the biggest reasons I’m running for Congress is because I want Iowa to be the best place in the country to help that potential grow. | = Peter, If you ever ask me what set me on the course for a good future, my answer will always be the same: Public schools and teachers gave me every opportunity I’ve ever had. I am who I am today because educators saw potential in me, pushed me to do better, and held me accountable when I needed it. When an educator invests in a student, it can change the entire course of their life. Every single child carries boundless potential, and one of the biggest reasons I’m running for Congress is because I want Iowa to be the best place in the country to help that potential grow–to be number one in education again. That’s why last week meant so much to me. I had the chance to visit City High and speak with an American government class. The students were so thoughtful and engaged that I forgot I was talking to high schoolers and not my law students. They asked smart questions and reminded me just how bright our future can be. But here’s the hard truth: Iowa is ranked 23rd in education. That didn’t happen by accident. While our schools struggle for resources, Mariannette Miller-Meeks has done nothing to turn things around. She has supported diverting public education funds to private entities, voted for policies that threatened the jobs of up to 145,000 teachers and school staff, and backed cuts totaling more than $35 million from public education funding. This is unacceptable. In Congress, trust that I will be a champion for public education, and if anyone dares to go against Iowa's public schools, I. Will. Raise. Hell. name: David Hogg
subject: No regrets
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Stepping away from the DNC changed everything.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260205-1&t=1&akid=3122%2E587540%2Eda3C1j)
A year ago, I was elected DNC Vice Chair.
I ran for this volunteer role for a very simple reason. After the election, I attended my first DNC Executive Committee meeting to hear what party leadership thought went wrong. A pollster presented on the loss, and the very first group she highlighted was 18–29-year-old voters.
**_I looked around a table of more than 30 committee members and didn’t see a single person under 30._**
In that moment, I realized I could either keep complaining about institutions like the DNC or step in and try to be the change I — and so many people my age — wanted to see. After endless hours on the phone and a relentless campaign, I was elected at 24.
During my time as vice chair, one truth became impossible to ignore: for decades, we’ve claimed we have a messaging problem. In reality, we have a _messenger_ problem.
To strengthen the party, we don’t need a new slogan — we need new, bold, young leaders who change what it means to be a Democrat.
So, I announced that Leaders We Deserve would challenge asleep-at-the-wheel incumbents in safe blue districts. Not to weaken the party but to strengthen it. To create accountability. To ensure that no seat is so “safe” that it excuses stagnation.
I could bore you to death about by-laws, and get into the nitty gritty of the “procedural” maneuver the DNC used to re-do the vice chair election, but for now, I’ll say this: that decision **_terrified_** the establishment.
So I chose not to seek re-election. And honestly? That decision unlocked everything.
Stepping away meant freedom. Freedom to fully focus on backing bold, forward-thinking leaders like Justin Pearson, Nida Allam, and Patrick Roath. Freedom to send Christian Menefee to Congress.
Freedom to challenge a political ecosystem that too often rewards consultants who make millions while campaigns lose the most consequential elections of our lifetime. Freedom to build something better.
Today isn’t a day for regret. It’s a day to reflect on what Leaders We Deserve has already made possible and the work still ahead.
Sometimes growth requires discomfort. Leaving the DNC freed me to act decisively, support real change-makers, and fight for a Democratic Party that actually resonates with voters. And the data is starting to show it — recent polling and youth turnout in Virginia prove young people are beginning to come back.
And **Peter,** none of this happens without you. Our candidates don’t take corporate PAC money. They don’t answer to special interests. They rely on grassroots supporters like you.
**[So if you believe in building a new generation of leaders who will challenge entrenched power, reimagine our party’s future, and actually deliver results, will you chip in $5 today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260205_1_dnc.ZjQAe6&refcode=em20260205-3122&amount=5&t=2&akid=3122%2E587540%2Eda3C1j)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260205_1_dnc.ZjQAe6&amount=5&refcode=em20260205-3122&t=21&akid=3122%2E587540%2Eda3C1j)**
I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve built together — and grateful for the more than 200,000 donors who give us the independence to do what’s right, not what’s comfortable.
Thank you for being part of this movement.
— David Hogg

name: Forward Party
subject: Election Reform Yes. Federal Election Takeover No.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Americans want elections that are easier to vote in and harder to mess with. That is a goal we share.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
Americans want elections that are easier to vote in and harder to mess with. That is a goal we share. Let’s start with an important truth. Our elections are not rigged at the ballot box. Votes are counted, audited, and checked. But the broader system is distorted in other ways, especially by discriminatory ballot access rules and structural barriers built by the two major parties that make it harder for independent and third-party candidates to compete. That is where reform is needed. The Constitution gives primary responsibility for running elections to the states. That was not an accident. It was a deliberate guardrail against concentrating too much power in one place. A decentralized system spreads risk, encourages innovation, and makes manipulation more difficult. It is far harder to tamper with 50 different state systems than it is to target one giant centralized one. Moving all election control to Washington would not strengthen trust or security. It would create a single point of failure and a single point of political control. Nationalizing elections would also tilt the playing field even further toward the two major parties. Today, third parties and independents can at least compete under varied state rules, with some states offering more accessible paths to ballot access and alternative voting models. A single national standard would almost certainly be written by and for the dominant parties, likely locking in stricter requirements nationwide and closing off those pathways. That is not modernization. That is consolidation. We absolutely support real election reform. That means making it easier for eligible citizens to vote, easier for candidates to run, and easier for voters to have real choices. It means fair ballot access rules, open competition, transparency, and strong security practices. What it does not mean is a federal takeover of election administration. Election reform should expand participation and trust, not concentrate power. When reform turns into control, voters lose. **Forward this to your friends, family, coworkers - helps us introduce them to Forward and what we are trying to build. We would also love it if you could invite them to one of our upcoming events listed below.**
---

So back to changing the system... We are excited about the huge, warm reception that the first episode of our newly announced podcast received! Since we're on a roll with these announcements, we have another one: We have rebranded our podcast and settled on a final name: The Forward Party Podcast. This is more descriptive and searchable and better captures the breadth of content and ideas we will be bringing to you over the coming months. Thank you for all the feedback! Now on to even more exciting things: The next episode of The Forward Party Podcast is now live! In this second episode, hosts Lindsey Drath, Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, and Lt. Gov. Kerry Healey explore a shared question shaping American civic life right now: How do we rebuild trust, restore dialogue, and lead without falling into partisan traps? The conversation brings together two distinct voices who approach that challenge from different angles, yet land on strikingly similar conclusions about leadership, speech, and responsibility. First to join them in the discussion is journalist and author Rikki Schlott, a columnist for the _New York Post_ and co-author of _The Canceling of the American Mind_. Drawing from her reporting and personal experience as a Gen Z writer navigating today’s campus climate, Rikki offers a candid look at how free speech debates, social media incentives, and institutional failures are shaping young people’s political identities. The episode then turns to Minnesota, where Mike Newcome, a Forward Party candidate for governor, joins the conversation. Mike brings a practical lens shaped by decades as a business leader and his current campaign. We hope you enjoy! clean_body: Americans want elections that are easier to vote in and harder to mess with. That is a goal we share. | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — Americans want elections that are easier to vote in and harder to mess with. That is a goal we share. Let’s start with an important truth. Our elections are not rigged at the ballot box. Votes are counted, audited, and checked. But the broader system is distorted in other ways, especially by discriminatory ballot access rules and structural barriers built by the two major parties that make it harder for independent and third-party candidates to compete. That is where reform is needed. The Constitution gives primary responsibility for running elections to the states. That was not an accident. It was a deliberate guardrail against concentrating too much power in one place. A decentralized system spreads risk, encourages innovation, and makes manipulation more difficult. It is far harder to tamper with 50 different state systems than it is to target one giant centralized one. Moving all election control to Washington would not strengthen trust or security. It would create a single point of failure and a single point of political control. Nationalizing elections would also tilt the playing field even further toward the two major parties. Today, third parties and independents can at least compete under varied state rules, with some states offering more accessible paths to ballot access and alternative voting models. A single national standard would almost certainly be written by and for the dominant parties, likely locking in stricter requirements nationwide and closing off those pathways. That is not modernization. That is consolidation. We absolutely support real election reform. That means making it easier for eligible citizens to vote, easier for candidates to run, and easier for voters to have real choices. It means fair ballot access rules, open competition, transparency, and strong security practices. What it does not mean is a federal takeover of election administration. Election reform should expand participation and trust, not concentrate power. When reform turns into control, voters lose. Trump lost Georgia in 2020.

We have to triple down on voter mobilization and voter protection.

body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2409%2E135344%2EfLB03a)

In November, myself and five other Members of Congress made a video quoting current law, that the military has a responsibility to refuse illegal orders.
In response, President Trump tweeted more than a dozen times, calling for me to be investigated, arrested, and hanged.
Since then, the FBI and former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, now U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me for the inquiry.
I wanted to share an important update on all of this, and ask for your help.
Earlier today, I wrote to Attorney General Pam Bondi and U.S. Attorney Pirro to inform them that I won’t be doing an interview -- and that their offices should preserve their records should I decide to sue for their infringement on my Constitutional rights.
I am not going to legitimize what they’re doing. The video in question was public, and I’ve talked about it extensively in the open. Our Constitution is crystal clear about our freedom of speech – and that’s a value worth fighting for.
To be honest, very smart people have told me to keep my head down and be quiet – that doing so would make this inquiry go away. But that’s exactly what Trump and Pirro want. They are employing physical and legal intimidation to get me to shut up. And, much more importantly, to deter other people from criticizing them.
So I’m taking the opposite approach, and I am fighting back, because this is bigger than any one Senator or any one video. If they can do this to me, what can they do to a business leader or the head of a community foundation or a mom who goes viral on the internet for criticizing Donald Trump?

name: AOC
subject: It's time to know your neighbor.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Believe it or not, building community — whether it's your church, mosque, a knitting group, your dinner circle — is far more transformative than you realize.
If you don’t know your neighbor, it’s time to know your neighbor.
If you have a co-worker you think you’re cool with, it’s time to get to know that person.
It’s time to get to know the people we will be relying on to protect each other.
It may seem frivolous, but I guarantee you it’s not: **creating community around you is one of the most powerful and radical things you can do in an environment like this**.
Sometimes even just being in community with people who are not like-minded with you — is a very odd little thing that can help change their mind.
We have no choice but to live in the times that we live in, and to make it better one day at a time, one choice at a time.
**Never, ever think that any choice or act of yours is too small. It isn't.**
Regimes and autocracies are taken down by millions of drops of small actions that would otherwise be invisible by masses of people.
This is the assignment that we have ahead of us. I look forward to doing this work with you all.
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260205.rNP_0M&refcode=em20260205-10736-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10736%2E2526796%2Er0ohKJ)
Our main project now is to **unite the working class in this country against a fascist agenda**. Period.
[Help us continue the fight by making a grassroots donation.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260205.rNP_0M&refcode=em20260205-10736-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10736%2E2526796%2Er0ohKJ)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260205.rNP_0M&refcode=em20260205-10736-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=10736%2E2526796%2Er0ohKJ)**
In solidarity,
Alexandria

warnings

nationalize elections is all about getting the SAVE Act passed – a bill
that would lead to mass voter suppression ahead of the 2026 midterms. Now,
Senate Republicans are already plotting to bring the bill up for a vote
and could try to sneak it into a must-pass funding package any day.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35126?source=email-20260205&t=1012&akid=10178%2E5885482%2EUjUKGX ]Make no mistake: this bill is one of the biggest threats to voting
rights in a generation. We CANNOT allow Congress to pass this bill – but
it’s going to take ALL of us to stop it. Take action right now: Add your
name to demand Congress OPPOSE the SAVE Act.

everyday Americans who want their voices heard. It would require voters to
present a passport, birth certificate, or naturalization papers just to
register or re-register to vote. It would directly undermine free and fair
elections, disproportionately impacting communities of color, young

In a moment, I'm going to ask you to split a donation between me and Trisha Calvarese to be a Founding Donor to my campaign. Please give me a chance to explain why it's so important:](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001H57GZw-dfmC9oa00ZYg7lV641xmLkBvYmZmS0yYZP3h4cpR4ECF_FLmPwAbfJBChmmipUQujo7qzT4OF3nXIzzsN-xdpviNbc0SdPdwwpl_52FA9ZZPuYRtC-JHSuwr7mHsEfAvKWyvGq0NIuyBNGkadyFgKx7dCSBMeFu-n6Nxbd2uPUy5mfzsLhxOkk7G_MHIiaZAGI4HQ4uzflvAL0DRGqVRwQ9ht&c=xYtF38kq14_j7H6-aQ_qTpyuURDd9GHyUjSph9GKgctRH6mwdGw_Xg==&ch=cUzgOcmdOm576GZAQA2EA2TcD6fk1KAKmfoX0StToK6dahsErdRnYA==)
I never thought I'd have to defend our democracy from a violent mob inside the Capitol building.
I joined the Capitol Police 16 years ago because I wanted to serve and protect the place where our democracy happens. I swore an oath to protect the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic.
I could have never expected that oath would lead me to fight Donald Trump's insurrectionists on January 6th, 2021.
For hours, I was immersed in a profane mix of sweat, screams, shrieks, anger, death, fear, blood, broken limbs, spit, hatred, horror, racism, and bigotry as Trump's violent mob attacked my fellow officers and tried to overturn a free and fair election.
Donald Trump did NOTHING to stop them. For three hours, he watched on TV while we were beaten bloody.
But I had confidence that I could stand strong. I knew that this is America, and here, we stand for what's right.
[If you're ready to be on the right side of history, join me and Trisha Calvarese in our fight against Trump today. Chip in anything you can. Every dollar will help take down his House Majority, and together, we can defend our democracy:](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001H57GZw-dfmC9oa00ZYg7lV641xmLkBvYmZmS0yYZP3h4cpR4ECF_FLmPwAbfJBChmmipUQujo7qzT4OF3nXIzzsN-xdpviNbc0SdPdwwpl_52FA9ZZPuYRtC-JHSuwr7mHsEfAvKWyvGq0NIuyBNGkadyFgKx7dCSBMeFu-n6Nxbd2uPUy5mfzsLhxOkk7G_MHIiaZAGI4HQ4uzflvAL0K_hK2-Ee1PL&c=xYtF38kq14_j7H6-aQ_qTpyuURDd9GHyUjSph9GKgctRH6mwdGw_Xg==&ch=cUzgOcmdOm576GZAQA2EA2TcD6fk1KAKmfoX0StToK6dahsErdRnYA==)

| A lot has happened since that day in 2021.
I testified before Congress about what really happened. I spoke truth to power while some of the same people I protected tried to rewrite history and pretend it was just a "normal tourist visit."
I've endured relentless attacks from Trump and his MAGA supporters. They've called me every name in the book. They've threatened my family. They've threatened me.
But I still believe that we must stand up for what's right.
Now, Donald Trump is back in the White House with unchecked power.
His ICE agents are terrorizing communities with masks and military weapons -- just like his insurrectionists did on January 6th. The only difference is that now they're being paid with your tax dollars.
His MAGA enablers in Congress are letting him treat the Constitution like it's optional. They're ignoring subpoenas. They're refusing oversight. They're acting like Trump is a king instead of a president.
And I'm not going to sit back and let it happen.
That's why I'm running for Congress, Peter.
Because my oath to protect and defend the Constitution didn't end on January 6th. It will never end.
Our country has lived through challenging periods before. We've overcome, persevered, and moved toward a more perfect union. We're in the middle of another fight for our country right now.
I still have faith that good can prevail over evil and that we can overcome these hard times. What is right still matters here... but only if we make it matter.
I'm ready to continue this fight in Congress. I know Trump and his MAGA machine inside and out. I've faced them before. I stood strong when it mattered most.
[But I need you to stand with me now. If you're fired up to take down Trump's House Majority and hold him accountable, it would be an honor to have your support as a Founding Donor. | | | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

clean_body: What 2025’s wins mean for 2026 | = Peter, remember Election Day 2025? Back on November 4, EMILYs List women delivered a clean sweep — and it wasn't just a feel-good headline. It was a blueprint for how we take back power in 2026. The 20 Democratic pro-choice women who won or advanced in November's elections proved that EMILYs List women are at the center of the fight to take back power: EMILYs List women secured a Democratic trifecta in Virginia — with Abigail Spanberger as governor, Ghazala Hashmi as lieutenant governor, and our TEN House of Delegates candidates flipping Republican seats. Mikie Sherrill won a hard-fought race to become New Jersey’s next governor, defeating her MAGA Republican opponent, and now ready to address the challenges facing her community. Justice Christine Donohue retained her seat on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court — helping to hold the court's progressive majority for years to come. And in cities across the country, voters elected Democratic pro-choice women mayors to lead their cities forward. These women are powerful models of what it looks like to run and win in tough races, and we're proud to stand by them. Fellow American —

I want to be completely candid with you about what we’re walking into this year. The 2026 midterms are not routine — they’re shaping up to be a referendum election, and Democrats are already operating like they can taste the Speaker’s gavel again. Republicans hold the House right now, but our majority is razor-thin, and we cannot afford even a small slip in turnout, enthusiasm, or resources.

The hard truth is Democrats don’t need a “wave.” **They don’t need 30 seats. They only need a handful to flip control of Congress, and they’re building their entire strategy around that reality.** They’re targeting competitive districts nationwide, recruiting challengers, and using every headline they can to fuel small-dollar fundraising and motivate their base.

And we all know what happens if Democrats take the House. Deporting criminal illegal aliens is shutdown. We’ll be fighting tax increases instead of delivering tax cuts. And crazy Leftists will run all the committees. **Instead of results, Washington becomes a circus again — investigations, subpoenas, political stunts, and endless obstruction designed to paralyze President Trump’s final two years in office.** If Democrats flip the House, the America First agenda is dead on arrival.

That’s why I’m reaching out today. We have a narrow window to build the resources we need early so we can define this race on our terms, win the air war, and fund a serious turnout operation before Democrats’ outside money starts flooding in.

clean_body: They only need a handful to flip control of Congress, and they’re building their entire strategy around that reality. | Fellow American — I want to be completely candid with you about what we’re walking into this year. The 2026 midterms are not routine — they’re shaping up to be a referendum election, and Democrats are already operating like they can taste the Speaker’s gavel again. Republicans hold the House right now, but our majority is razor-thin, and we cannot afford even a small slip in turnout, enthusiasm, or resources. The hard truth is Democrats don’t need a “wave.” They don’t need 30 seats. They only need a handful to flip control of Congress, and they’re building their entire strategy around that reality. They’re targeting competitive districts nationwide, recruiting challengers, and using every headline they can to fuel small-dollar fundraising and motivate their base. And we all know what happens if Democrats take the House. Deporting criminal illegal aliens is shutdown. We’ll be fighting tax increases instead of delivering tax cuts. And crazy Leftists will run all the committees. Instead of results, Washington becomes a circus again — investigations, subpoenas, political stunts, and endless obstruction designed to paralyze President Trump’s final two years in office. If Democrats flip the House, the America First agenda is dead on arrival. That’s why I’m reaching out today. We have a narrow window to build the resources we need early so we can define this race on our terms, win the air war, and fund a serious turnout operation before Democrats’ outside money starts flooding in. We’ve worked too hard to let the radical left claw their way back into power and turn Congress into an emergency brake on President Trump’s agenda, fellow American. Thank you, Beth Van Duyne | | PAID FOR BY BETH VAN DUYNE FOR CONGRESS

Friend, I know we've asked for your support a lot in recent months.

We've asked because it's truly vital — because there's a national bullseye on our race, because this seat is one of the top MAGA targets in the nation, and because we're relying on our grassroots donors to help us defend it.

But I want you to know that we never, ever take your support for granted. When you invest in our race, you're investing in our democracy. You're investing in our fight to flip the House and deliver a better future for working people everywhere.

Your investment in our campaign is so meaningful, and I can't overstate how moved, humbled, and deeply grateful I am to have you with me, friend.

Together, I know we can continue delivering big victories for Northern Ohio — like lower healthcare and prescription drug costs, stronger environmental protections, and an economy that finally works for workers.

Thank you so much, friend, for powering our work this month. We wouldn't be here without you.

— Marcy

**Early voting for the primary election begins today -- Illinois voters are officially starting to make their voices heard at the ballot box.**

I’m criss-crossing Central and Southern Illinois, meeting folks who are worried about the chaos in Washington. Worried about the affordability crisis -- from the rising cost of living, to home prices, and sky-high healthcare premiums.

While I’ve managed to secure wins for IL-13 despite MAGA control, it’s clear that we need accountability in the form of a Democratic House majority.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 2/5/2026
body:
Parents allege school mistreatment of autistic child as Cherry Creek faces federal civil rights investigation
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are confronting the fallout from years of [one-time federal funds used to during COVID](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to create permanent government obligations, worsening Colorado’s budget shortfall and renewing scrutiny of TABOR. That [tension surfaced during SMART Act hearings](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), where agencies struggled to defend rapid budget growth, Medicaid expansion, rising fees, and weak oversight. At the same time, a House immigration resolution exposed [sharp divides over sanctuary policies](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with Democrats pressing back against federal enforcement and Republicans warning of higher taxpayer costs.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Education, public safety, and governance remain under pressure as [Cherry Creek School District faces a federal civil rights investigation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over alleged mistreatment of an autistic student. A Jefferson County school is also accused of [teaching students to track ICE agents](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), fueling backlash over activism in classrooms. The state confirmed its [14th wolf death since reintroduction](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), [former Denver Police Chief Paul Pazen](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) entered a City Council race focused on public safety, and a new commentary warns that [top-down “15-minute city” planning](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) clashes with Colorado’s geography and culture of personal freedom.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** National debates are sharpening as the American Society of Plastic Surgeons urged [delaying gender-related surgeries until age 19](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), citing insufficient evidence and child safety concerns. Meanwhile, Congress narrowly [ended a government shutdown](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), setting the stage for a high-stakes fight over immigration enforcement and DHS funding.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, February 5, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Parents allege school mistreatment of autistic child as Cherry Creek faces federal civil rights investigation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
In response to concerns raised by a family in Colorado about the treatment of their young son in kindergarten, the Office for Civil Rights of the U.S. Department of Education opened an investigation into whether the Cherry Creek School District was in compliance with federal civil rights and special education law, a problem that is not new to the district.
The concern was raised after months of unanswered questions, the parents said.
Ana and Brandon Lantz’s son started kindergarten in 2023. As time went on in the school year, records indicate that their son received special instruction outside of the general classroom. At first, it was small group instruction. Then, it was one-on-one instruction.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Lawmakers admit the problem: One-time money built permanent government](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY CORY GAINES, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Lawmakers admit one-time federal funds created permanent government growth:** Legislative staff now acknowledge that billions in temporary COVID-era dollars were used to expand ongoing programs, directly contributing to Colorado’s structural budget shortfall.
* **TABOR restrained deeper damage—but lawmakers worked around it:** The article argues that without TABOR’s limits, spending would have grown even faster, noting how legislators increasingly relied on fees, reclassifications, and loopholes to bypass voter-approved constraints.
* **Government expansion outpaces private growth with little remorse shown:** Data highlighted in the commentary shows state government spending and employment have grown far faster than the private sector, while lawmakers largely defend the choices rather than reconsider them

**[Lawmakers press agencies as SMART Act hearings expose budget growth and policy shifts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY COLLEEN ENOS, [CHRISTIAN HOME EDUCATORS OF COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **SMART Act hearings expose runaway spending and weak accountability:** Lawmakers pressed agencies that struggled to justify rapid budget growth, rising licensing fees, and expanding Medicaid costs, confirming concerns that state government has grown faster than oversight.
* **Weiser’s lawsuits and DEI priorities draw scrutiny:** Attorney General Phil Weiser revealed Colorado has spent roughly $600,000 on 51 lawsuits against the Trump administration, while DEI remains a core departmental focus despite potential risks to federal funding.
* **Auditors flag fraud, parole failures, and Medicaid abuse:** State auditors cited $25 million in Medicaid fraud, a 39% spike in health facility licensing funds without supporting data, and unresolved failures in DOC parole risk assessments.

[****](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | FEBRUARY 3** _“There’s a lot of candidates running and I know there’s a lot of confusion out there about who conservatives in the area should be supporting,” said James Ruehmann, president of the Turning Point USA chapter at CMU. With more than 20 Republicans in the governor race, and the field wide open until the primary election on June 30, Coloradans on the Western Slope have few opportunities to hear candidates gathered together to discuss how they’d lead the state._
____
[**Medicaid billing error cost Colorado tens of millions, officials acknowledge**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)[****](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**BY CORY GAINES | COMMENTARY | FEBRUARY 3** _State officials acknowledged that a Medicaid billing error caused Colorado to overpay tens of millions of dollars to contracted providers, with projected savings of nearly $33 million this year and more than $60 million next year once the mistake is corrected._
__
[**DUI arrest tests public trust as Aurora councilman keeps safety oversight role**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) **BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | FEBRUARY 2** _When an elected official is arrested, the expectation is simple: the law should apply the same way it would to anyone else. But public office brings added scrutiny that doesn’t disappear once the legal process begins._[****](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)__

### Mutual aid needs memory. Which is why, in the thick of everything, you should still read *Service and Sacrifice.*
| | [Melissa Chaudhry](https://substack.com/@melissa4congress)

We are living in a season where everyone is triaging.
People are exhausted. Families are stretched. ICE is expanding, and community is doing emergency work--rides, childcare, food, legal funds, rapid response. In times like this, reading can feel like a luxury.
So here's the honest question: **Why should you give your scarce attention to** _**Service & Sacrifice**_**right now?**
Because we're not only fighting policies. We're fighting for the **soul of the Republic**.
Mutual aid keeps people alive. But a people also need something else to survive: **a shared definition of courage**. A living memory of what integrity looks like when the state, or the crowd, or the institution demands cowed obedience.
This is a book about that.
Yes, it contains documented facts--years of them. Yes, it traces how a machine tries--and fails!--for decades to grind a family to powder. But the beating heart is simpler and older:
**When empire asks you to help harm the innocent, do you comply --or do you refuse?**
That question belongs to every culture that has survived domination. It belongs to every language and country of origin. It belongs to every faith community and every labor tradition. And in America, it's the founding energy of our nation's existence: resistance to tyranny, insistence on dignity, and the fragile project of self-government.
Benjamin Franklin put the whole wager in one line: **" A republic--if you can keep it."**
Keeping it isn't a vibe. It's a practice. And sometimes it's a price.
### The courage this story records
My husband, Muhammad Zahid Chaudhry, is a **100% service-disabled U.S. Army veteran** --wheelchair-bound from injuries sustained on active duty.
He did what we claim to honor in America: he treated his oath to uphold the Constitution as binding.
When pressured by government agencies to participate in wrongful surveillance and to help frame innocent people as "terrorists," he refused. Not because it was safe. Because it was right.
For that refusal--for that integrity--he endured a 25-year campaign of institutional retaliation that ultimately culminated in an act designed to break him: he was illegally abducted at a citizenship appointment and held in ICE detention for 124 days, including a full week in solitary confinement.
This is not a story about a paperwork error. It's a story about **what authoritarian systems do with principled people**.
### Why the book matters now
Authoritarianism doesn't always arrive with tanks. Sometimes it arrives with "routine procedure," with quiet coercion, with the normalization of cruelty, with incentives to look away.
What stops it is not only elections. It is **character, community, and a refusal to be recruited into complicity**.
That's why this book has landed the way it has. A reviewer wrote:
> "Service & Sacrifice is one of those rare books that stays with you long after you put it down... She weaves together biography, history, and moral insight... exposing how bureaucracy and bias can quietly erode the ideals we hold sacred."
Another reviewer called it:
> "a dense legal case... made humane, accessible, and infuriating... [showing] the value of immigrants, idealism, and the Rule of Law."
And readers have reflected that impact in a way that helps this story travel: the book has a **straight 5-star review history** , and it achieved **#1 Top New Release in four categories**.
### Resistance across cultures: the oldest American DNA
This book is also an immigrant story--yes. But not in the flattened, sentimental way America likes to consume.
It's an _immigrant-and-veteran_ story about the shared hunger that makes people risk everything: **the belief that a nation can be governed by principle rather than by fear.**
Immigrants and veterans are often the people who believed most deeply in the promise. That's why betrayal hits them like a theft of meaning.
If you're organizing right now, you know this: communities survive repression by building material support _and_ moral clarity. They survive by keeping memory alive. They survive by telling the truth, without euphemism, until the truth becomes a bridge between strangers.
That's what I wrote this book to do.
### Zahid is available to speak
Zahid is willing--after everything he's endured--to speak publicly about detention from the inside and about integrity under pressure: keynotes, panels, and as a moderator. His talks are not therapy sessions; they're civic witness and strategic clarity--what it means, and what it takes, to **keep a republic** when institutions are built to profit from suspicion, coercion, incarceration, and control.
Invite him: https://zahidc.carrd.co/
### Two clean ways to help
1. **Get the book + share it**

* Order (Amazon + non-Amazon options): [linktr.ee/justice4zahid](https://substack.com/redirect/140a2eb4-d40c-4f9e-b1f2-22176e0777a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

2. **Invite Zahid to speak**

* Speaker page + booking: [zahidc.carrd.co](https://substack.com/redirect/e09e7106-e601-4154-8da8-bf669c0a234a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Friends - we don't just need to "make it through." We need to uplift the integrity, principles, and spirit of America at all costs. This story helps us all remember how.
Stay safe out there. Stay strong. Stay sane. Stay connected.
With love and fire,
Melissa

# MEMORANDUM

To: Valued Supporters
From: Michael Biundo & Derek Dufresne, Partners – Ascent Strategic
Date: February 5, 2026
Re: Lily Tang Williams – Record-Breaking Fundraising Momentum & Why It Matters in NH-02

Dear Valued Supporters,

Lily Tang Williams is proving something important in New Hampshire’s 2nd Congressional District: when you speak plainly about the issues that actually affect working families, the support follows, and it follows fast.

In 2025, Lily raised over $532,000 from donors. Every dollar came from individuals, small businesses, families, and Americans who believe in her message. In addition, with her own $120,000 personal loan to the campaign, total receipts reached over $652,000. That donor-raised number puts her ahead of every other Republican running for the U.S. House in New Hampshire this cycle in non-candidate, grassroots-raised dollars. She enters 2026 with more than $507,000 cash on hand, built almost entirely from donor support. She views that personal loan as her own investment in getting the fundraising operation up and running early, a down payment that helped turn thousands of supporters into donors.

On the spending side, the campaign used approximately $278,000 in 2025. Much of that went directly towards the costs of raising funds: email fundraising, digital advertising, direct mail, events, and outreach that turned interest into contributions. That is a normal and necessary part of building a strong donor base from the ground up, and the results speak for themselves: strong, sustained support from people across New Hampshire and beyond.

Even though she currently faces no challenger in the NH-02 Republican primary, Lily’s fundraising performance already surpasses that of congressional candidates in New Hampshire’s 1st Congressional District. Her lead in donor-raised money and cash-on-hand shows the kind of early momentum that matters most, the kind built from real people.

Her fundraising strength and her strong showing last cycle, when she was the Republican nominee, have so far kept a real primary challenger at bay. In a state like New Hampshire, where the primary is one of the latest in the country (typically early September), that deterrence is huge. It gives her a massive head start: more time to build an organization, more resources to reach voters, and more runway to lock in support before anyone else can mount a serious campaign.

She is also far ahead of where past Republican nominees in NH-02 stood at this same point in their cycles. At the end of the year before the election, previous non-incumbent nominees typically had $0 to $100,000 in cash on hand. Lily’s $507,000 puts her roughly 5 to 10 times ahead of the next-closest historical benchmark for this stage, a clear sign of the strength she is bringing to the table early.

NH-02 hasn’t been uncompetitive; rather, it’s been unchallenged. The margins we’ve seen are the product of minimal investment, not structural safety. In midterm elections, the district’s large share of undeclared voters, rural and exurban communities, and lower-propensity Democratic turnout create a fundamentally more volatile electorate than top-line results suggest. With real resources and a credible candidate, NH-02 tightens quickly, often faster than NH-01, because fewer voters are locked into partisan voting patterns and persuasion still meaningfully moves the outcome.

This is not her first time exceeding expectations. In 2024, as a candidate with no prior elected office, Lily over-performed every realistic forecast in the NH-02 Republican primary. She earned strong support across the district, outperforming predictions despite running against opponents with far more name recognition and institutional backing. That experience proved she can connect with voters and build real momentum, and the numbers in 2025 show she’s doing it again, even stronger.

She grew up under communism in China. She came to America with nothing, built a business from the ground up, and raised a family here. She knows what it feels like when government gets too big, too expensive, and too far removed from the people it’s supposed to serve. That background is not just biography. It is why she fights the way she does. And it is why regular people are stepping up to back her.

New Hampshire’s 2nd District is more Republican-leaning than many places, but do not let that fool you. The same entrenched interests, the same insider games, and the same refusal to listen to everyday taxpayers exist here too. Lily is running into many of the same hurdles any outsider faces when challenging the status quo: well-funded opponents, establishment networks, and a system that often rewards longevity over results.

Yet she has already built the strongest non-candidate fundraising operation among NH Republicans running for Congress this cycle, both in money raised and money in the bank. That matters. It means she can reach voters directly, tell her story without apology, and compete on the issues that actually keep Granite State families up at night: inflation, energy costs, border security, and government that spends like it is someone else’s money.

Every dollar Lily has raised is going towards one goal: making sure the people’s voice is heard louder than the lobbyists’ and the career politicians’. She is not asking for special treatment. She is asking for accountability. And the response from donors across New Hampshire and across the country shows that message is landing.

We are still early in this cycle, but the foundation is already stronger than almost anyone expected. To keep that momentum going, to make sure Lily has the resources to fight the fights that need to be fought, we need your help now.

If you believe New Hampshire deserves a representative who puts families first, who understands what real struggle looks like, and who will never forget where she came from, then please consider joining us with a contribution today.

Donate securely at:
[https://www.lilytangwilliams.com/congress/donate/](https://lilytangwilliams.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=8317033781a524f5f640e7e3e&id=dcebf6376c&e=c338950e03). For larger gifts, or to discuss matching opportunities, reach out to either of us directly by email at _[Michael@Ascent-Strategic](mailto:Michael Biundo <michael@ascent-strategic.com>)_ and _[Derek@Ascent-Strategic.com](mailto:Derek Dufresne <derek@ascent-strategic.com>)_.

Thank you for standing with Lily. This is not just about winning an election. It is about restoring a government that actually works for the people again.

Sincerely,

Michael Biundo & Derek Dufresne
Partners
Ascent Strategic

Yet she has already built the strongest non-candidate fundraising operation among NH Republicans running for Congress this cycle, both in money raised and money in the bank. That matters. It means she can reach voters directly, tell her story without apology, and compete on the issues that actually keep Granite State families up at night: inflation, energy costs, border security, and government that spends like it is someone else’s money. Every dollar Lily has raised is going towards one goal: making sure the people’s voice is heard louder than the lobbyists’ and the career politicians’. She is not asking for special treatment. She is asking for accountability. And the response from donors across New Hampshire and across the country shows that message is landing. We are still early in this cycle, but the foundation is already stronger than almost anyone expected. To keep that momentum going, to make sure Lily has the resources to fight the fights that need to be fought, we need your help now. name: Rep. Jonathan Jackson
subject: A Reflection From the National Prayer Breakfast
body:
Dear Friend,
This morning, I had the honor of offering a prayer at the National Prayer Breakfast. I spoke from the heart about something I believe deeply—that leadership in this moment must be rooted in humility, clarity, and the courage to do what is right, even when it is difficult.
Our country is facing real and lasting challenges. Families in our communities are feeling the pressure of rising costs, uncertainty, and a political climate that too often rewards division instead of solutions. clean_body: I don’t trust what I’m seeing | Fellow American, When it comes to polling, there’s certain organizations you simply can’t trust. I know that better than anyone... That’s why it’s so vital that we conduct our own polling, especially when there’s a discrepancy with the numbers like what we’re seeing right now. On one hand, polling shows voters prefer Republicans over Democrats on nearly every key issue: National Security: Immigration: Foreign policy: Trade: National debt: But at the same time, polling by the mainstream media shows Democrats have surged out to a whopping on the generic ballot for the midterms. Something doesn’t add up... But the only way to do that is to have EVERY Republican and swing voter verify their voter profile before the upcoming verification deadline. name: Roy Cooper
subject: I can’t get to Washington alone
body:
I have a record of winning fights for the people.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=494%2E124072%2EEumNzT)
Peter, when we win this race and I head to Washington to serve as the next Senator from North Carolina, here’s what I plan to do:
* Speak up for the people whose health care costs skyrocketed because the federal government decided to slash health care benefits and give the rich a tax break instead
* Defend the values we share — respect for our democracy, the importance of the rule of law, the right to bodily autonomy, and more — no matter who is attacking them
* Prioritize finding real solutions to the challenges facing communities across the country by investing in public education, working to lower housing costs, and stopping the ridiculous trade wars that are driving up prices at the grocery store

These commitments are just common sense, Peter. They’re the same policies and priorities I worked for when I served as Governor of North Carolina. In NC, we passed Medicaid Expansion which got more than 700,000 more folks covered, got raises for public school teachers, and helped build a clean energy economy that brought good jobs to our communities. **I know you share many of these priorities, and I know you want politicians to do more than talk the talk — you want your elected leaders to put in the work. I have a record of winning tough fights for the people, and I’m ready to get back to work, but I can’t make it to Washington alone.** **[Peter, we’re aiming to earn 10,000 contributions before our critical FEC filing deadline on Wednesday so we can show everyone that the grassroots momentum is on our side. Can you pitch in $5 or more right now to meet this goal and help send me to Washington to fight for you?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5295?amount=5&t=7&akid=494%2E124072%2EEumNzT)** | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5295?t=8&akid=494%2E124072%2EEumNzT)
---
Let’s do this,
Roy
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5295?t=9&akid=494%2E124072%2EEumNzT)
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

#
Friend, I don’t need to tell you that Congress can be chaotic at times _(ok, pretty much all the time)._ But I’m fighting for mid-Michigan every day because we still have the power to deliver – and over the past year, we’ve been able to bring $126 million in grants to mid-Michigan, help hundreds of families and seniors cut through red tape, keep the Saginaw Social Security office open – and more. Look, there’s still a lot to fix. There’s a lot more to do. That’s why this race matters. And with election year underway, I want to let you in on our plan to keep this seat blue:

|
Peter,
The streets of Chicago feel right different now.
Unmarked vans prowl at night--masked ICE agents snatching neighbors in silence. Protesters are dragged across pavement by masked federal agents whose names are hidden behind black tape. Soldiers march through city intersections meant for kids on bikes and buses to work.
At food banks across America, recently laid off workers wait in line. Families scrape together meals as grocery prices skyrocket.
Children fall asleep hungry. Seniors cut their pills in half, praying it's enough to last the week.
This is Trump's America--and it's only been 12 months.
But in November, there was a beacon of hope.

Friend,
We crossed the red line with ICE long ago.
Even before the killing of American citizens Alex Pretti and Renee Good, ICE was an unaccountable federal agency focused on deporting immigrants by any means necessary.
ICE had a policy of separating children of immigrants from their parents at the US-Mexico border and still continues to put detainees in conditions that violate human rights standards.
Kevin Kiley wants you to believe that CA-03 voters stand with him in this cruelty—so I had my team put together a petition to prove just how wrong he is. Will you add your name to join the list of people standing with us against Kevin Kiley and ICE? [https://forms.oneswitchboard.com/heidi-hall-for-congress/ice]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://forms.oneswitchboard.com/heidi-hall-for-congress/ice]
Friend, I worked to prevent hazardous waste dumping by corporations along the US-Mexico border because I wanted to protect people and prevent things like children being born with birth defects.
So to Kevin Kiley, who voted to fund ICE, and all the Democrats who don't believe in abolishing this agency:
Who is protected when 32 people die in ICE custody in 2025 and 6 already this year?
Who is protected when children and their parents are kidnapped off the street with no due process and detained in facilities with conditions so bad that measles outbreaks take place?
This situation is despicable, and we need our leaders to start treating this with the urgency it deserves .
Friend, will you sign our petition and join us in showing Kevin Kiley that we won't sit idly by as ICE continues to wreak havoc on our communities? [https://forms.oneswitchboard.com/heidi-hall-for-congress/ice]
SIGN ON [https://forms.oneswitchboard.com/heidi-hall-for-congress/ice]
In solidarity,
Heidi Hall
Heidi Hall has spent her three-decade public service career working with others to solve problems, protect our land and water, improve health, and build opportunities for others, all while raising two boys primarily as a single mom.

Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.

This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
