There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.

2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:
Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/advocacy-groups-offer-training-for-pa-primary-poll-watchers/]
Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide/]
Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [https://fcfreepresspa.com/poll-workers-needed-for-pennsylvanias-2025-primary-election/]
6. Engage Your Elected Officials
Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.
7. Vote in Every Election
Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.
Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th!

Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [] The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests. In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [] . [] We are hiring! Let's provide civic education together! We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania. Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote! Positions start at $20 an hour. Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org] EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org] News You Can Use There are things every one of us can do [] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last. 1. Educate Yourself Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally. Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more. New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [] Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [] Everything you need to know about mail voting [] , becoming a poll worker [] Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [] Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [] , vetting judicial candidates [] Guides to State College school board [] , Reading City Council president [] Guides to voting as a college student [] En Español Guía para votar por correo [] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [] * Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [] 2. Stay Engaged To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win. Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [] ) 3. Share What You Learn Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting. Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year! 4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work. Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above! 5. Become a Trained Poll Worker Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process. Here are some resources that may be helpful: Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [] Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [] Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [] 6. Engage Your Elected Officials Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise. 7. Vote in Every Election Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility. Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th! Recent Events [] Solidarity for Immigrants On Monday, May 5th, also Cinco de Mayo, over 300 people, representing 18 community organizations from across Pennsylvania, gathered at the State Capitol in Harrisburg to rally for immigrant rights. We amplified voices that have been silenced, advocated against injustice, and showed that solidarity is not just a word—it is a force that creates change. This event was a declaration that Pennsylvania stands against injustice and division. [] [] [] NPPEF on the Ground [] Last Monday, May 5th was the last day to register to vote for the primary election! Our teams were out in their communities leading up to the voter registration deadline on Monday. We helped folks ensure they have the ability to exercise their right to vote in the primary on Tuesday, May 20th. Our teams are currently getting ready for GOTV - a time of year where we are on the ground connecting with our communities and mobilizing them to vote. It's our favorite time of year to build relationships with those we hope to uplift. Dauphin County [] [] Delaware County [] [] Luzerne County [] [] Super voters vote twice a year, every year ! Thank you for doing your part to stay informed and engaged! body:
I have two HUGE updates to share from Judicial Watch’s fight for election integrity, both of which are thanks to your loyal support.

|

| [ |
--- ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=79424&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU5vbi1Eb25vcnMmdXRtX3Rlcm09TWF5&hash=24ba264bf954565daeac2ee37d0d2a82cb50b51bf88688fefb7acd5ba4a0eade)

| Dear Fellow American,

We just scored another _HUGE win for clean elections_ :
Following **Judicial Watch 's federal lawsuit** to clean up voter rolls in Oregon, officials there have announced they will begin the process of **removing 800,000 dirty names from the state 's voter rolls**.
That's 800,000 fewer opportunities for voter fraud...which means that **Judicial Watch** lawsuits brought under the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) have now been **responsible for removing 5.8 million invalid names from voter rolls nationwide**.

| Now more than ever, we need to reaffirm our Constitutional rights and prohibit the president from weaponizing the federal government against people who disagree with him.
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9508%2E5257348%2Eh7nnaM)
Friend,
Donald Trump’s reaction to the second killing of an American citizen by federal agents in Minnesota has been entirely predictable. Instead of directing his Department of Justice to conduct a full investigation of the agents involved, he sicced them after the state's Democratic officials, including Gov. Tim Walz, Attorney General Keith Ellison, Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey, and Rep. Ilhan Omar.
He has populated the Justice Department leadership with cowards and toadies. He’s turned the Justice Department into both a sword to go after the president’s enemies and a shield to hide his corruption.
When Trump took office for his second term, I committed to standing up to him anytime he abused his power, sought to undermine our democracy, or divide this country. That has been a tall order from day one.
In his first year alone, he has unleashed unthinkable attacks on our democracy. From purging prosecutors at the Justice Department who refused to engage in unethical conduct, who put the rule of law above the rule of the person at the president’s desk, to these bogus attempts to prosecute his perceived enemies, including me.
_I’m not going to be intimidated by anything he says, by anything he does._
Someone has to stand up to this abuse of power, to defend our country and its people. Someone has to fight back. I have and I always will. Because this fight isn’t over. It’s just beginning, and I won’t back down.

subject: There’s a shift happening in Texas right now
body:
Democrats have been winning since November because Texans are desperate for something better.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I was on CNN this week talking about what we’re seeing on the ground here in Texas, and I want you to hear it directly from me.
Something **big** is happening in Texas.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260205_1_cnn.nwCYjd&refcode=em20260205-534&t=1&akid=534%2E299639%2EI8u6X_)

And it’s happening all across Texas, from big cities to small local races, grassroots organizing and real conversations are driving results. Democrats have been winning since November because Texans are desperate for something better.
In Tarrant County, the Latino vote shifted dramatically. We are seeing the same energy across the state as voters reject the status quo and demand leadership that improves our lives. We have seen this before. In 2018, Beto O’Rourke won 64 percent of the Latino vote in Texas. When I get 64 percent of the Latino vote in November, I will win. 2018 was the proof of concept; 2026 is the win. That’s what’s possible when we show up. And now it is time to finish the job.
With less than 30 days left until the primary, we have to keep building this momentum. We can win in November if we do it together. Every conversation and every supporter matters.**

— Gina

clean_body: I'm the biggest obstacle to their agenda = I’m guessing you got involved in politics for the same reason that I did: You believe that elections have real consequences. Personally, I prefer to focus on the positive consequences of winning an election. Protecting and restoring our Constitutional rights. Bringing down costs for families across Kansas. Keeping our communities safe from violence. Giving our kids the education they deserve. But we can’t ignore the negative consequences. And in a year like this? Those consequences could be enormous. The Kansas GOP even spent this past weekend plotting it all out at their Winter Convention. We don’t know what their 2026 platform looks like yet... but if it’s anything similar to 2024? We’re talking about an all-out abortion ban, a ban on same-sex marriage, and ripping away health care from those who need it most. subject: My thoughts on what’s happening in New Hampshire
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Chris Pappas is in a tied race — and Republicans are coming hard for this seat.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260205_2.LE-Sox&refcode=em20260205-2&t=1&akid=4975%2E582294%2EvY8ngI)
Hi, it’s Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear.
There’s a lot of noise in an election year — I know that better than most. But let me be very clear: **The Senate race in New Hampshire could decide the direction of this country.**
Chris Pappas is running in a tied race. It could be a toss-up. And with Donald Trump in the White House, the stakes couldn’t be higher.
**[That’s why I’m asking you to chip in $5, or anything you can, right now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260205_2.LE-Sox&refcode=em20260205-2&t=2&akid=4975%2E582294%2EvY8ngI)**
The first year of this second Trump Administration has seen chaos, division, and dangerous rollbacks of basic freedoms. That’s why it’s so important we elect leaders like Chris Pappas — leaders who know how to bring people together, deliver real results, and never forget who they’re fighting for.
Chris’s opponent is a former U.S. Senator with national name recognition and the backing of national Republicans and their deep-pocketed super PACs. Republicans believe they can flip this seat and block any chance we have of checking Trump’s power in Washington.
But I believe in Chris — and I believe we can win.
Chris understands that leadership isn’t about grabbing headlines or scoring political points. It’s about showing up, listening, and doing the hard work to deliver for working families. He’s done that in Congress, and I know he’ll bring that same spirit of public service to the Senate.
Kentucky and New Hampshire may look different, but our constituents are people who want the same things: good jobs, strong schools, access to health care, and a future we can build together. That’s what Chris Pappas is fighting for. **_But he can’t do it alone._**
**[If you’re with me — and ready to stop Trump and his allies from flipping this critical seat — chip in now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260205_2.LE-Sox&refcode=em20260205-2&t=3&akid=4975%2E582294%2EvY8ngI)**

Let’s get Chris across the finish line.

Andy Beshear

From the devastating shooting deaths of American citizens in Minneapolis to unconstitutional detentions and attacks on legal residents, one thing has become painfully clear: **The Department of Homeland Security is being run without oversight. And Congress can’t afford to stay quiet.** No accountability. No transparency. No answers for the families left behind. **[That’s why I’m co-sponsoring a resolution to impeach DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. If the President won’t act, Congress must. **[But it starts here -- with accountability at the top. Peter, we need to talk about why Republicans across the country, who know they can’t win fairly in November, are trying to change the rules of democracy. Let’s zoom in on Missouri. First, state Republicans passed an unpopular gerrymander to try to rig the midterm elections in their favor. Then, more than 300,000 Missourians signed petitions to challenge this egregious map with a statewide referendum. That’s when Republican officials started throwing more hurdles in their way — arbitrarily throwing out petition signatures and crafting deliberately confusing ballot language. It’s part of a trend. Republican state officials are cracking down on citizen-led reform initiatives — pushing higher vote thresholds to pass ballot measures, manipulating ballot language, burying the petition gathering process in red tape, and even working to overturn or ignore results. clean_body: Help us defend democracy as Republicans crack down on voter-led referendums for fair maps. | Peter, we need to talk about why Republicans across the country, who know they can’t win fairly in November, are trying to change the rules of democracy. Let’s zoom in on Missouri. First, state Republicans passed an unpopular gerrymander to try to rig the midterm elections in their favor. Then, more than 300,000 Missourians signed petitions to challenge this egregious map with a statewide referendum. That’s when Republican officials started throwing more hurdles in their way — arbitrarily throwing out petition signatures and crafting deliberately confusing ballot language. It’s part of a trend. Republican state officials are cracking down on citizen-led reform initiatives — pushing higher vote thresholds to pass ballot measures, manipulating ballot language, burying the petition gathering process in red tape, and even working to overturn or ignore results. Voters are fighting back against these concerted anti-democracy efforts — and we must do everything we can to support them. In February 2025, a JP Morgan executive named Gregg Smith was sentenced to two years in federal prison. His crime? For eight years, he manipulated gold and silver prices through "spoofing." Thousands of fake orders. Prices driven down. Then canceled milliseconds later. The Department of Justice called it "racketeering." **JP Morgan paid $920 million. They need our prayers & our voice

Peter,
I want to take you back in history for a moment, and you’ll very quickly understand why.

Forty-seven years ago, in the shadow of Soviet tanks and communist oppression, Pope John Paul II stepped onto Polish soil for the first time in thirty-one years and spoke three simple words:

_**“Be not afraid.”**_

Millions had gathered there in Warsaw’s Victory Square. The regime trembled. And within a decade, the Berlin Wall lay in rubble.

**Paired together with courageous political leadership from Ronald Reagan and Margaret Thatcher,_faith – spoken boldly – had triumphed over fear._**

Today, that same spirit is under siege – not in Poland, but in places like **Nigeria, Sudan and even South Korea.**

**Consider Leah Sharibu, a brave 15-year-old Christian schoolgirl in Nigeria.** In 2018, Islamic State barbarians abducted 110 girls from her school. While 104 were returned and five tragically killed, they kept Leah – as punishment for her **unyielding refusal to renounce Christ and convert to Islam.** Now, many years later, she remains in captivity with ISWAP (Islamic State West Africa Province), who threaten to hold her as a "slave for life."

And yet, this is just one example facing Christians in Nigeria. Since 2009, there have been a reported **19,000 churches destroyed** , **over 100,000 killed** and **at least 5 million more displaced.** The data reveal that for every one Muslim, 5.2 Christians are killed.

**In Sudan** , Islamist paramilitaries known as the Rapid Support Forces have been on a rampage, **bombing churches** , and **killing priests and worshippers sheltering inside while forcing survivors to convert or be killed** – in some cases, **_crucified_**. **Over 150,000 have died in the conflict, many hunted and targeted for their faith.** This ongoing conflict has resulted in a catastrophic humanitarian crisis, including mass displacement, severe food insecurity, and the complete collapse of public services.

**In South Korea** , a nation we rebuilt and have defended for 75 years, the new government with communist sympathies has been **arresting pastors, seizing church records, and even jailed an 82-year-old religious leader for leading prayer.**

And if you think this is only an international problem, I ask you to think back just a couple of years, when **pro-life grandmothers – _women in their 70s and 80s_ – were handcuffed and imprisoned by Joe Biden’s DOJ for peacefully praying outside abortion clinics.**

I don’t share these tragic, gruesome facts to paralyze you with despair, but to rally you to act. And here’s how...

**Save the Persecuted Christians** is an organization that has been effectively fighting on the front lines of this battle – **leading a 200+ group coalition to amplify survivors’ voices, awaken the public and policymakers, and drive direct action to hold the perpetrators accountable.**

In fact, they played a key role in the successful effort to encourage President Trump to designate Nigeria as a “Country of Particular Concern” (CPC), officially laying the groundwork for targeted sanctions and other measures.

[**As you read this, they’re in the midst of a nationwide fundraising campaign to support their efforts at home and across the globe, and I urge you, as strongly as I can:_Be Not Afraid_. clean_body: They need our prayers & our voice | | | | | Peter, I want to take you back in history for a moment, and you’ll very quickly understand why. Forty-seven years ago, in the shadow of Soviet tanks and communist oppression, Pope John Paul II stepped onto Polish soil for the first time in thirty-one years and spoke three simple words: “Be not afraid.” Millions had gathered there in Warsaw’s Victory Square. The regime trembled. And within a decade, the Berlin Wall lay in rubble. Paired together with courageous political leadership from Ronald Reagan and Margaret Thatcher,faith – spoken boldly – had triumphed over fear. Today, that same spirit is under siege – not in Poland, but in places like Nigeria, Sudan and even South Korea. Consider Leah Sharibu, a brave 15-year-old Christian schoolgirl in Nigeria. In 2018, Islamic State barbarians abducted 110 girls from her school. While 104 were returned and five tragically killed, they kept Leah – as punishment for her unyielding refusal to renounce Christ and convert to Islam. Now, many years later, she remains in captivity with ISWAP (Islamic State West Africa Province), who threaten to hold her as a "slave for life." And yet, this is just one example facing Christians in Nigeria. Since 2009, there have been a reported 19,000 churches destroyed , over 100,000 killed and at least 5 million more displaced. The data reveal that for every one Muslim, 5.2 Christians are killed. In Sudan , Islamist paramilitaries known as the Rapid Support Forces have been on a rampage, bombing churches , and killing priests and worshippers sheltering inside while forcing survivors to convert or be killed – in some cases, crucified. Over 150,000 have died in the conflict, many hunted and targeted for their faith. This ongoing conflict has resulted in a catastrophic humanitarian crisis, including mass displacement, severe food insecurity, and the complete collapse of public services. In South Korea , a nation we rebuilt and have defended for 75 years, the new government with communist sympathies has been arresting pastors, seizing church records, and even jailed an 82-year-old religious leader for leading prayer. And if you think this is only an international problem, I ask you to think back just a couple of years, when pro-life grandmothers – women in their 70s and 80s – were handcuffed and imprisoned by Joe Biden’s DOJ for peacefully praying outside abortion clinics. [1]Justice Democrats

The 2026 Democratic primaries are here: early voting has officially begun
in Illinois, Peter!

While incumbent Justice Democrat Rep. Delia Ramirez is unopposed in her
primary, we’ve got a progressive, working-class candidate running for the
open seat in IL-08: Junaid Ahmed.

And AIPAC is already spending through new secret PACs for his corporate
opponent:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260205-ja.FhaxQA&refcode=em20260205-37438&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=37438%2E1203867%2E8rQbk3 ]Tweet by Akela Lacy: Missed this: Illinois Playbook reporting something
I’ve been hearing — that AIPAC is behind the new ads today for Donna
Miller in IL-02, Melissa Bean in IL-08 and Laura Fine in IL-09 run by two
PACs, Elect Chicago Women and Affordable Chicago Now

Junaid is a community leader and small-business owner running to stand up
to the Trump administration and Israel lobby to turn the page on corporate
special interests who put profits over people.

He’s spent his life rolling up his sleeves: volunteering after natural
disasters, distributing food to families in need, organizing, and fighting
corporate greed. In Congress, Junaid will fight to abolish ICE, stop
funding Israel’s genocide in Gaza, and pass bold policy solutions like
Medicare for All.

Junaid is going up against multiple corporate candidates in this crowded
race, including one former Congresswoman who has taken hundreds of
thousands of dollars from AIPAC’s friends in the Israel lobby and now has
their quiet backing in this election.

This opponent was even called “Wall Street’s Favorite Democrat.” The

Yesterday’s
judicial hearings were a sham.

Trump’s nominees were handed the softest possible test — questions about
reality: Who won the 2020 election? Was January 6 an attack on the U.S.
Capitol?

And once again, they refused to answer.

These nominees chose to avoid historical fact and hide behind rehearsed
non-answers and legal wordplay — dodging any answer that might upset
Trump.

Senator Richard Blumenthal called it what it was:

“I am insulted as a member of this body that you won’t tell us the truth...
You’ve all been carefully rehearsed... I think you failed the test.”

He’s right. They failed — deliberately.

These nominees are demonstrating loyalty. They’re signaling that they’ll
protect Trump’s lies, excuse political violence, and stay silent when
democracy is attacked, all in exchange for a lifetime seat on the bench.

And here’s the most enraging part... Nineteen Senate Democrats have voted to
confirm these judges.

Nineteen. Let that sink in.

And every vote “yes” helps pack the courts with Trump cronies — judges who
won’t defend elections, won’t condemn insurrection, and won’t protect our
rights when it counts.

Demand Justice PAC is done pretending this is normal. We’re calling out
the nominees and the Democrats enabling them. Because letting this slide
is how democracy erodes.

Hey folks,
I went live with Scranton Mayor **Paige Cognetti** to discuss corruption, broken systems, and what it actually looks like to govern for people. If you care about beating corruption and taking back the House, you need to watch this.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:06**] Paige breaks down what Governor Shapiro's endorsement means -- and why rooting out corruption has defined both of their careers.
* [**00:04:05**] How Paige took on (and beat) a deeply entrenched political machine in Scranton -- as an independent.
* [**00:07:01**] The receipts on Rob Bresnahan's stock trading scandal -- trading on votes while families pay the price.
* [**00:13:00**] Why the Epstein scandal is about more than one man -- and what it reveals about power protecting itself.
* [**00:17:57**] Why mayors make better leaders -- and why Washington desperately needs people who know how to actually govern.

This conversation is about more than one race. It's about whether we're willing to finally say **enough** -- enough corruption, enough insider games, enough politicians using public office to enrich themselves. Paige has beaten corruption before, and she's ready to do it again in Pennsylvania's 8th. If you value honest leadership and real accountability, help me keep conversations like this going.

---
| | **A NOTE FROM CHRISSY**
---
| | **ICE, DHS, and KRISTI NOEM**
---
The world is watching in horror as Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents operate recklessly, dangerously, and lawlessly in Minnesota and elsewhere. Earlier last month, they fatally shot Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti and detained a 5-year-old boy returning home from preschool.

I voted recently against additional funding for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) because ICE isn’t operating legally, transparently, or with accountability. I, along with all of my Democratic colleagues in Pennsylvania, urged Sens. Fetterman and McCormick to push for reforms to DHS and to vote against this bill unless the reforms are added. Lastly, I am calling for the impeachment of DHS Secretary Kristi Noem for high crimes and misdemeanors.

My duty is to our community, and I will not give the Trump administration a blank check to endanger its own citizens.
---
| | **ACA Tax Credits Celebration**
---
As you know, I’m a champion for affordable health care because health care is a right, not a privilege. Despite pleas from economists, health care professionals, their constituents, and those of us on the other side of the aisle, Republicans in Washington failed to prevent ACA tax credits from expiring on Dec. 31. The cost for health insurance and health care went up significantly for millions of Americans on Jan. 1.

Because of the backlash from people like you (thank you!), Speaker Mike Johnson was forced to allow the House to vote on a three-year extension of these credits, and 17 GOP lawmakers joined all House Democrats in voting to pass this bill.

Now, it's the Senate's turn to pass this extension without delay. How can you help? Keep the pressure on your Senators to pass this bill. Let’s get this done.
---
| | **don't give up the ship video update**
---
The FBI has transferred the investigation to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, which is run by lawyer, author, and Fox News host Jeanine Pirro. There is no basis for it, but given how vengeful this administration is, I am still taking this seriously. In response to the video, the Pentagon withdrew a defense policy fellow they had previously placed in my office, and there are calls to have my security clearance revoked.

Free speech has never been more important. Holding those who break the law accountable has never been more important. All of us doing our part to preserve our values and our democracy has never been more important.

I took an oath to the Constitution when I joined the Air Force and again as a member of Congress. I am upholding my oath and will continue to do so.
---
| | **My Friends, the governors**
---
Two of my closest friends in Congress – Mikie Sherrill and Abigail Spanberger – were just sworn in as the new Governors for their states. I attended both inaugurations and could not be happier for them or more certain that the people of New Jersey and Virginia are in the right hands.

Wins like these remind us that even during the most difficult times, Democrats are still prevailing, fighting steadily against the MAGA extremism plaguing our country. I'm thrilled knowing the people of New Jersey and Virginia are getting a friend and a real leader as their Governor.
---
Thank you for your support, Derek.

There's work to be done,

Chrissy

This isn’t a White House. It’s not a presidency. These are not serious public servants. This is a heist. Everything Trump does has one goal: Take people’s money.
#

Peter, maybe you’ve heard: Trump is suing the IRS.
He’s asking for $10 BILLION in damages. He wants the American taxpayer to give him $10 billion — after he’s already pocketed something like $5 billion off the presidency over the course of his first year in office.
It’s about as clear an example of corruption as you’ll ever see.
Scott Bessent sat before me in a hearing today. He’s not only the Treasury Secretary, but the acting director of the IRS, too. He’s the guy who will transfer those funds to Trump. So, I asked him about it.
Watch the video here:
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/3302?t=1&akid=4069%2E734936%2EfATU8i)
This isn’t a White House. It’s not a presidency. These are not serious public servants. This is a heist. Everything Trump does has one goal: Take people’s money — taxpayers, billionaires, foreign governments, investors, even his own die-hard supporters.
We’ve never seen anything like this in the history of our country, and I’m not going to stand for it.
I am going to keep holding Trump’s feet to the fire. I am going to fight like hell against this in the Senate. And I’ll be campaigning all year to help win back majorities in Congress this November.
That’s the only way to stop this and hold him accountable.

| | I hope this email finds you and your family well. I'm truly grateful for the incredible support we're seeing across Michigan as we build toward the March endorsement convention and beyond.
**Huge news on election integrity** — a top priority for all of us! Yesterday, it was reported that the signatures threshold was met to put the **Citizen-Only Voting Amendment** on the November ballot. That means Michigan voters will finally get to decide: Should only U.S. citizens vote in our elections? The answer is a resounding **YES**!
But let's not stop - even more petition signatures would be great to **create a buffer and ensure it passes in a landslide** with the Michigan Secretary of State. Every petition signature counts to secure our elections and protect your vote. [I recorded a quick message about how you can still help and you can view by clicking below](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=4a752f3ea6&e=4b10910eed):
[****](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=de1345375d&e=4b10910eed)
Help finish strong! Haven’t signed yet? Now’s the time. Already signed?**Help spread the word**. Go right now to [**MichCOV.com**](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=417e21dc3e&e=4b10910eed) to learn more about signing and sharing it with your family, friends, and neighbors. Let's flood the Secretary of State with support and secure our elections! Every petition signature counts, every voice matters.
As Michigan’s next Attorney General, **I’ll fight to secure our elections and defend this constitutional amendment to victory**. Your right to vote as a citizen should be defended against those that seek to harm our way of life. Huge thanks to every volunteer and signer who made this happen - let’s finish the job strong, gather extra petition signatures, and **vote YES for Citizens-Only Voting** this November! 🇺🇸

We can’t settle for half measures.

Peter,
The results of our 2026 Priorities Survey are in. Last week, we asked thousands of you to tell us what you want to see from the progressive movement in 2026, and the message is clear.
**Here’s what we heard in the survey:**
_“We want Democrats to push back harder against Trump and the Republican agenda — not hedge, not compromise away our values, and not stay silent while people are harmed.”_
_“We need Democrats to stop ICE’s terror. The unlawful raids, kidnappings, detention deaths, and violence happening without due process, and to defund an agency that is out of control.”_
_“We need you to protect health care for everyone, including reproductive care, trans people, immigrants, and working families.”_
_“Democrats need to use every tool available to protect people’s lives and rights. No more half measures when the stakes are this high.”_
**And more than any single issue, you told us that the old way of doing things isn’t going to cut it.**
People want leaders who are willing to think bigger, move faster, and fight harder. Leaders who will stand with working people instead of billionaires, and with communities instead of corporations.
That’s why Pramila’s focused on growing and training the progressive movement, standing up to Trump’s authoritarian agenda, and taking back the House this year so we can actually deliver on the change people are demanding. But she can’t do it alone.

name: Christopher Ahuja for Congress
subject: Justice for Survivors Can’t Wait. The Powerful Must Be Held Accountable.
body:
We must demand justice for Epstein's survivors

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=f905a41eae&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,Across the country, painful stories are surfacing, stories that remind us how often powerful systems have failed girls and women. Epstein survivors who were ignored, silenced, or treated as disposable are asking for what should never have been denied in the first place: dignity, safety, and justice.This is a moment in our nation’s history unlike any other, and those responsible for the unconscionable acts against children, girls, and young women in the Epstein pedophilia ring are clearly monsters. Every female (and all people) deserve to live free from exploitation, coercion, and abuse. Every survivor deserves to be believed, supported, and protected. The Epstein victims, those with us and those no longer with us, were abused and forgotten by a powerful elite mob of criminals. Accountability is a must, regardless of status or connections.In California and across the nation, we have seen how culture can normalize harm or help lead positive change. Artists, storytellers, organizers, and advocates have played a powerful role in changing how our society confronts abuse, amplifies survivor voices, and demands structural reform. That work is far from finished.As your candidate for Congress in CA-32, I believe that protecting girls’ and women’s rights is imperative as a basic human rights issue. That means strengthening laws that hold abusers accountable, supporting survivor-centered justice systems, expanding resources for prevention and recovery, and building a culture where dignity is non-negotiable.This campaign stands unapologetically with survivors, and with everyone determined to stop the powerful from exploiting the vulnerable.[**With your support, we will strengthen protections, elevate every overlooked voice, and demand accountability from those in power.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=2b352f2f9c&e=53c7d12fc7) Justice will be served. And together, we will fight relentlessly for dignity, safety, and justice for all.

Trump lost Georgia in 2020.

The President called on Republicans to nationalize and “TAKE OVER” elections (!)

This immediately after the FBI — alongside Tulsi Gabbard, the nation’s spy chief — RAIDED a Georgia election office and seized truckloads of 2020 ballots.

From Minnesota to Georgia, we are watching the President unravel as he abuses federal power to pursue vendettas and consolidate power.
